author: Solao
description: Buff manager: casts what you can cast, quaffs the highest-level potion for what you can't.
script:
--[[
    aw-spellup.lua
    Sean Stoves (Solao) — 2026-08-07

    Buff manager. Two halves that answer one question: this buff is down, what
    now?

    Cast it, if you can. The MUD's own 'spellup' already decides what to cast
    and refuses the rest — mana, recoveries, nomagic rooms, sleeping, combat,
    mutual exclusions, forgetskill. It knows all of that better than a client
    ever will, so the casting half of this sends exactly one command and never
    'c <skillnum>'.

    A cast always wins. Not "usually", not "unless mana is short" — always,
    and for a reason that outranks every other consideration in here: a spell
    you cast lands at YOUR level, and a potion lands at the potion's. At 201
    that is not close. So a potion is what happens when there is no cast to be
    had, and the only three things that count as that are not having the spell,
    never having practised it, and the MUD saying you don't know it.

    Quaff it, if you can't. That is the half worth building. A potion carries
    its own spell level — 'Eyes of Allegiance' is a level 4 item that casts
    level 15 detect good — so among the potions that grant a buff, the one with
    the highest SPELL level is the one to drink, and the item's level has
    nothing to do with it.

    The join between them is the skill table. Every tag identifies a spell by
    number, a potion's affect arrives as the same {affon} a cast produces, and
    'slist spells' is what turns a number into a name. One table, both halves.

    Written from docs/aardwolf-spelltags.md, which was written from Aardwolf's
    published protocol and a live slist. Hadar's MUSHclient plugin showed the
    idea was worth having and contributed the queue-until-standing shape; no
    code came from it.

    WHAT IS PROVEN AND WHAT IS NOT, because the difference has cost time:

    The tag half is cross-checked against that plugin, which is in daily use.
    'tags spellups on' is its documented install step, and its {affon},
    {affoff}, {sfail} and {recoff} patterns are the same as the ones here.
    Treat those as settled.

    The skill table and the 'aff' sync are NOT in that plugin — it never reads
    either, because it casts by skill number and so never needs a name. Both
    are this port's own, and both are where the failures have been: the 'aff'
    header it waited for turned out not to be text Aardwolf prints at all.
    So anything in those two paths is an assumption until a live session says
    otherwise, which is what 'awbuff raw' exists to answer.

    THE POTION TABLE IS THIS PLUGIN'S OWN.

    aw-loot is never consulted while this runs. Not for stock, not for levels,
    not for keywords. It holds a lot of identify boxes and there is a button to
    copy the potions out of them once, and that is the entire relationship — a
    button you press, not a lookup in the hot path. Uninstall the Loot Tracker
    and nothing here changes behaviour.

    What stops it emptying your bag:

    A sync gate. {affon} only fires on a fresh cast or quaff, so everything
    already running when you log in is invisible to the tag stream. Without
    reading 'aff' once, the first tick sees every buff as down and drinks a
    potion for each. Auto does nothing until a sync has happened.

    The run cap. A potion that goes down and grants nothing would otherwise
    loop until the bag is empty — 'help quaff' says certain spells only work
    from an object if your class can cast them. An earlier version tried to
    blame the individual potion for that and switched it off after two misses;
    a live session disproved the premise, switching off a Shadowbane that then
    granted detect hidden for 7:28 when quaffed by hand. So the cap ends the
    RUN rather than accusing a row, which is the claim the evidence supports.

    And the usual: off by default, one quaff in flight, a gap between them, a
    run cap.

    Aardwolf allows assist tools and not unattended automation. The Mudlet
    version gated on the AFK flag from its who poller; there is no such signal
    here, so the gate is that auto is off until you turn it on, it only ever
    reacts to something dropping, and the cap ends a run rather than letting it
    go all night. Said out loud in 'awbuff help' rather than left implied.

    The command is 'awbuff'. 'spellup' belongs to the MUD and registering it
    here would eat it — see MUDFORGE-NOTES #13.
]]

-- @category widgets

plugin = {
    id          = "aw-spellup",
    name        = "Aardwolf Spellups",
    version     = "1.12.0",
    author      = "Solao",
    description = "Buff manager: casts what you can cast, quaffs the highest-level potion for what you can't.",
    settings    = { saveState = true },
}

--[[
    Drop every handler already on a widget event.

    Looked up through _G rather than called by name: a global this build does
    not have throws on the way IN, before pcall can catch anything, so a bare
    reference would take the plugin down on any client that lacks it.
]]
local function drop_handlers(id, event)
    local ok, fn = pcall(function() return _G["unregisterWidgetEvent"] end)
    if ok and type(fn) == "function" then pcall(fn, id, event) end
end


local TAG  = "$Y[Spellups v" .. plugin.version .. "]$w "
local TAGR = "$Y[Spellups]$w "

local VAR  = "aw_spellup_cfg"
local SKV  = "aw_spellup_skills"
local POTV = "aw_spellup_pots"

--[[
    Off by default and it stays that way through an install. Every other panel
    in this set reads the game and draws it; this one drinks potions you paid
    for and spends mana. A plugin that starts doing that because it was
    installed is a plugin that empties a bag while you read its help.
]]
local cfg = {
    on        = false,      -- act by itself
    threshold = 5,          -- how many spellups down before 'spellup' goes out
    cooldown  = 45,         -- seconds between 'spellup' sends
    gap       = 4,          -- seconds between potions
    cap       = 8,          -- potions in a row without the picture improving
    low       = 2,          -- potions left before it tells you to go shopping
    login     = true,       -- read the skill table and 'aff' once you're in
    potions   = true,       -- may it spend potions by itself
    prefer    = "cast",     -- cast | level; see next_potion
    combat    = false,      -- act while fighting
    bag       = "",         -- potion bag keywords
    view      = "buffs",    -- buffs | pots | set
}

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- state
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local skills = {}       -- skillnum -> { name, target, duration, prac, recovery, type }
local byname = {}       -- lowercase name -> skillnum
local recov  = {}       -- recoverynum -> name

local affect = {}       -- skillnum -> expiry epoch
local hasdur = {}       -- skillnum -> true once a real {affon} carried seconds
local blocked = {}      -- recoverynum -> expiry epoch
local failed = {}       -- skillnum -> { code, at, recovery }
local dropped = {}      -- skillnum -> when it fell off
local nope   = {}       -- skillnum -> true, the MUD says you don't have it

local synced   = false  -- has 'aff' been read since login
local lastFire = 0      -- when 'spellup' last went out
local lastQuaff = 0     -- when a potion last went out
local run      = 0      -- potions in a row
local quiet    = false  -- stood down
local backoff  = 0      -- resting/sitting; sit it out rather than spinning

--[[
    The MUD had nothing to cast.

    "No spells or skills cast." is Aardwolf saying the spellup did nothing at
    all, and re-sending on the next cooldown just asks the same question again.
    Sit out a while: something has to actually drop before the answer changes,
    and an {affoff} clears this.
]]
local castDead = 0
local DEAD_FOR = 120

--[[
    A cast failed for a reason that will not last. Try again when it clears.

    Aardwolf says WHY, and each reason has one right answer — that table is the
    whole reason a tag-driven caster beats a keybind that fires the same list
    blind. Hadar's MUSHclient plugin does the same thing and retries exactly
    codes 1, 6 and 10, queueing the rest until char.status says you are
    standing; this borrows the shape and answers with 'spellup' instead of
    'c <skillnum>', so the MUD still picks what to cast.

    retryAt is when we may try, and some codes ALSO need a condition met — no
    amount of waiting fixes "resting or sitting" if you are still sitting.
    retries caps a run of them, because a reason that never clears would
    otherwise re-send forever.
]]
local retryAt  = 0
local retryWhy = ""
local retries  = 0

local RETRY_MAX  = 3        -- in a row, before it goes back to normal pacing
local RETRY_GAP  = 6        -- seconds; a retry bypasses the cast cooldown, not this

-- code -> how long to wait before trying again
local RETRY_IN = {
    [1]  = 2,      -- lost concentration: immediate is fine
    [3]  = 0,      -- blocked by a recovery: {recoff} moves this along
    [4]  = 20,     -- not enough mana
    [5]  = 30,     -- nocast room; no room subscription here, so a plain wait
    [6]  = 5,      -- cannot concentrate, usually combat
    [10] = 5,      -- resting or sitting
    [12] = 20,     -- not enough moves
}

--[[
    The potion table. Keyed by the keyword string, because that string is both
    the identity and the thing that gets sent — two potions with the same
    keywords are the same potion as far as 'get' and 'quaff' are concerned.

        keys   "potion optical precision detectinvis see"
        name   "[Potion] Optical Precision"
        where  where you bought it, typed or read off the box
        level  the ITEM's level, which is only ever shown, never chosen on
        spells "5|detect invis~15|detect good" — the levels that DO get chosen on
        on     included in the automatic path
]]
local pots = {}

-- session only, never saved: what the MUD has told us since login
local stock   = {}      -- keys -> false once 'you do not have that item'
local qpend   = {}      -- keys -> when we sent it, cleared by the affect landing

--[[
    How many of each are left, counted rather than asked for.

    Aardwolf will tell you on request, but asking costs a 'look in <bag>' that
    scrolls thirty lines past you, and asking often enough to be current means
    doing that constantly. So the numbers are seeded from a listing when one
    goes by and then kept by subtraction: the MUD echoes 'You quaff <thing>'
    for every potion that actually goes down, ours or one you drank by hand.

    nil is honest — it means nobody has counted that one yet, and the panel
    says so rather than showing a confident zero.
]]
local count  = {}       -- keys -> how many are in the bag
local inBag  = false    -- inside a listing of OUR bag
local bagSaw = {}       -- ...and which of our potions turned up in it
local bagTmr = nil
local lowSaid = {}      -- already mentioned this one is running out

local QGRACE = 12       -- seconds a quaff has to draw the MUD's own echo

--[[
    How long a potion's buff is assumed to last until 'aff' says otherwise.

    A placeholder, not a guess about any particular potion: the only job is to
    stop the next tick quaffing a second one for a buff that just landed.
]]
local POT_GUESS = 45

--[[
    How long to leave the MUD before asking what landed.

    This was 2500ms and it caused the worst failure yet: eight potions in a row
    and a stand-down, with every buff actually up. The reply is AUTHORITATIVE —
    sync_done drops anything it does not list — so an 'aff' that arrives before
    the MUD has applied the potion does not merely miss the buff, it erases the
    optimistic mark that was holding the loop off. Everything reads as down
    again and the next tick quaffs another.

    Five seconds. The command queue has to drain, the potion has to take, and
    the reply has to come back; being early here is expensive and being late
    costs a couple of seconds of a panel showing an estimate.
]]
local POT_AFF_WAIT = 5000
local lastAff   = 0

local widget = nil

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- small stuff
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

local function trim(s)
    return (string.gsub(tostring(s or ""), "^%s*(.-)%s*$", "%1"))
end

local function low(s)
    return string.lower(trim(s))
end

local function now()
    return os.time()
end

--[[
    Read capture n out of a trigger callback.

    The callback is (captures, line, wildcards, raw) — captures FIRST. The
    wildcards table is keyed by the STRING "1", so it has no index base to get
    wrong; try that first. Captures may arrive 0- or 1-based, so the base is
    worked out ONCE from the table rather than guessed per lookup by trying n
    and falling back to n-1 — with two captures that guess hands back capture 2
    when asked for capture 1.
]]
local function cap(c, w, n)
    if type(w) == "table" and type(w[tostring(n)]) == "string" then
        return w[tostring(n)]
    end

    if type(c) == "table" then
        local base = (type(c[0]) == "string") and 0 or 1
        local v = c[n - 1 + base]
        if type(v) == "string" then return v end
    end

    return ""
end

--[[
    Takes a table, never varargs — those arrive undefined through the
    transpiler. Type check rather than truthiness, because undefined is truthy
    under Lua rules and every caller indexes what this returns.
]]
local function gmcp_get(names)
    for _, name in ipairs(names) do
        local d = getGMCPData(name)
        if type(d) == "table" then return d end
    end
    return nil
end

local function esc(s)
    s = tostring(s or "")
    s = string.gsub(s, "&", "&")
    s = string.gsub(s, "<", "<")
    s = string.gsub(s, ">", ">")
    s = string.gsub(s, '"', """)
    return s
end

-- MMM:SS, zero-padded so a column of them doesn't jitter as they count down
local function fmt(secs)
    secs = math.max(0, math.floor(tonumber(secs) or 0))
    return string.format("%d:%02d", math.floor(secs / 60), secs % 60)
end

--[[
    Split on one character, by hand.

    string.gmatch is available and Core uses it, but the transpiler runs Lua
    patterns through a JavaScript regex engine and which classes survive that
    is not something to be guessed at per call site. A character loop has no
    such question hanging over it, and these strings are short.
]]
local function split(s, sep)
    local out, cur = {}, ""
    s = tostring(s or "")

    for i = 1, string.len(s) do
        local ch = string.sub(s, i, i)
        if ch == sep then
            table.insert(out, cur)
            cur = ""
        else
            cur = cur .. ch
        end
    end

    table.insert(out, cur)
    return out
end

--[[
    Does the haystack contain this literal? Scanned, not searched.

    string.find(s, needle, 1, true) is supposed to be a plain search, and the
    plain flag does not survive: a needle carrying regex metacharacters comes
    back as no match at all. That is not hypothetical — "(!(Shadowbane)!)"
    kept its colour markers because "(!(" never matched, and "[Potion] Optical
    Precision" would never have been found in a bag listing because of the
    brackets. Both are exactly the names this has to match.

    A character walk has no pattern in it to be compiled wrongly.
]]
local function contains(hay, needle)
    hay, needle = tostring(hay or ""), tostring(needle or "")

    local hn, nn = string.len(hay), string.len(needle)
    if nn == 0 or nn > hn then return false end

    for i = 1, hn - nn + 1 do
        if string.sub(hay, i, i + nn - 1) == needle then return true end
    end
    return false
end

--[[
    An item's short description, as it would appear in a container listing.

    The identify box wraps a coloured name in (!( and )!) — "(!(Eyes of
    Allegiance)!)" — and that is a rendering marker, not part of the name. Left
    in, it is stored as the name and then never matches the same item sitting
    in the bag, so nothing gets counted and the strike message names a potion
    nobody recognises.
]]
local function clean_name(s)
    s = tostring(s or "")

    local out, i, n = "", 1, string.len(s)
    while i <= n do
        local three = string.sub(s, i, i + 2)
        if three == "(!(" or three == ")!)" then
            i = i + 3
        else
            out = out .. string.sub(s, i, i)
            i = i + 1
        end
    end

    return trim(out)
end

--[[
    'awbuff pot add "a b c"' and "awbuff bag 'potion bag'" mean what they look
    like. The quotes belong to what gets SENT — get "keys" "bag" — and typing
    them here is the natural thing to do having read that line, so they come
    off rather than ending up inside the keywords and being sent doubled.
]]
local function unquote(s)
    s = trim(s)
    local n = string.len(s)
    if n < 2 then return s end

    local a, b = string.sub(s, 1, 1), string.sub(s, n, n)
    if (a == "'" or a == '"') and a == b then
        return trim(string.sub(s, 2, n - 1))
    end
    return s
end

--[[
    The arguments, as words.

    The runtime hands over a table indexed from ZERO, or sometimes the raw
    string instead. Neither survives table.concat, and indexing the string form
    is no better — args[1] off "pot add x" is "p".
]]
local function argv(args)
    local out = {}

    if type(args) == "string" then
        local cur = ""
        for i = 1, string.len(args) do
            local ch = string.sub(args, i, i)
            if ch == " " or ch == "\t" then
                if cur ~= "" then table.insert(out, cur); cur = "" end
            else
                cur = cur .. ch
            end
        end
        if cur ~= "" then table.insert(out, cur) end
        return out
    end

    if type(args) ~= "table" then return out end

    local i = 0
    while args[i] ~= nil do
        table.insert(out, tostring(args[i]))
        i = i + 1
    end

    if #out == 0 then
        for _, v in ipairs(args) do table.insert(out, tostring(v)) end
    end

    return out
end

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- what the MUD says about you
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--[[
    char.status.state: 1 and 2 are the login sequence, 3 is standing about, 8
    is fighting. Sending during 1 or 2 lands in the name or password field,
    which echoes nothing — so a plugin that sends on connect just fails your
    login with no sign of why.
]]
local function state()
    local s = gmcp_get({ "char.status", "Char.Status" })
    if type(s) ~= "table" then return nil end

    local n = tonumber(s.state)
    if not (n and n >= 0) then return nil end     -- NaN is truthy; >= 0 is not
    return n
end

local function playing()
    local n = state()
    return n ~= nil and n >= 3
end

local function fighting()
    return state() == 8
end

--[[
    Your level. Needed because a potion has TWO levels and they do different
    jobs, which took a correction to get straight:

      Type : Potion       Level :  4      <- what YOU must be to drink it
      Spells : 1 use of level 15 'detect good'   <- how strong the buff is

    The spell level picks the best potion. The ITEM level decides whether it is
    on the table at all. At level 11 most of a high-level potion collection is
    simply unusable, and a picker that only looked at spell level would keep
    reaching for the one that gives the best buff and cannot be drunk.
]]
local function my_level()
    local st = gmcp_get({ "char.status", "Char.Status" })
    if type(st) ~= "table" then return nil end

    local n = tonumber(st.level)
    if not (n and n > 0) then return nil end
    return n
end


--[[
    THE STORE SURVIVES A REINSTALL. saveTable DOES NOT.

    saveTable and savePluginFile are scoped to the plugin, and a remove-and-
    re-add is how every update is installed — so each new version arrived with
    an empty skill table and an empty potion list, and the first thing you had
    to do was read 619 rows off the MUD again. That is not a cache, that is a
    chore with a cache-shaped hole in it.

    World variables outlive the plugin. aw-who worked this out the same way.

    Stored as tab-and-newline delimited text rather than JSON: what the
    transpiler does to nested tables through an encoder has bitten this
    codebase repeatedly, and a spell name contains neither a tab nor a
    newline. Fields are positional, so a row that does not have the right
    number of them is skipped rather than half-read.
]]
local function put_blob(name, text)
    pcall(function() setVariable(name, text) end)
end

local function get_blob(name)
    local ok, v = pcall(function() return getVariable(name) end)
    if ok and type(v) == "string" and v ~= "" and v ~= "null" and v ~= "undefined" then
        return v
    end
    return nil
end

-- rows of tab-separated fields; anything short is dropped, never guessed at
local function rows_of(blob, want)
    local out = {}
    for _, line in ipairs(split(tostring(blob or ""), "\n")) do
        if line ~= "" then
            local f = split(line, "\t")
            if #f >= want then table.insert(out, f) end
        end
    end
    return out
end

--[[
    The settings, in the same world-variable store as everything else, so a
    reinstall does not hand you back the defaults along with an empty table.

    Positional and fixed-width: a row with the wrong number of fields is
    ignored outright rather than half-applied, which is the behaviour you want
    the day this gains a field.
]]
local CFG_VAR = "aw_spellup_cfg_v2"

local function cfg_blob()
    return table.concat({
        cfg.on and "1" or "0",
        tonumber(cfg.threshold) or 5,
        tonumber(cfg.cooldown) or 45,
        tonumber(cfg.gap) or 4,
        tonumber(cfg.cap) or 8,
        tonumber(cfg.low) or 2,
        cfg.login and "1" or "0",
        cfg.combat and "1" or "0",
        cfg.bag,
        cfg.view,
        cfg.prefer,
        cfg.potions and "1" or "0",
    }, "\t")
end

local function cfg_load()
    local f = rows_of(get_blob(CFG_VAR), 11)[1]
    if not f then return end

    cfg.on     = (f[1] == "1")
    cfg.login  = (f[7] == "1")
    cfg.combat = (f[8] == "1")
    cfg.bag    = f[9]
    cfg.view   = (f[10] ~= "" and f[10]) or "buffs"
    cfg.prefer = (f[11] == "level") and "level" or "cast"

    -- default ON, so a row written before it existed keeps the old behaviour
    cfg.potions = (f[12] ~= "0")

    local keys = { "threshold", "cooldown", "gap", "cap", "low" }
    for i, key in ipairs(keys) do
        local n = tonumber(f[i + 1])
        if n then cfg[key] = math.floor(n) end
    end
end

local function save_cfg()
    saveTable(VAR, cfg)          -- the fast path, wiped by a reinstall
    put_blob(CFG_VAR, cfg_blob())
end

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- the skill table
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--[[
    'slist spells' reports duration = 0 for every row — sanctuary, fly and cure
    light alike — so that column is not a buff length and filtering on it would
    empty the panel. What actually separates a buff from an instant heal is
    whether the MUD ever announces an affect for it, which it only does for
    things that last. So it gets learned by watching: see hasdur.
]]
local SELF_OK = { [2] = true, [3] = true }      -- 2 = self or other, 3 = self only

local function is_spellup(s)
    return type(s) == "table" and s.type == 1 and SELF_OK[s.target] == true
end

local function skills_count()
    local n = 0
    for _ in pairs(skills) do n = n + 1 end
    return n
end

local function have_skills()
    for _ in pairs(skills) do return true end
    return false
end

--[[
    The skill table only changes when your class does, so there is no reason to
    pull 619 rows off the MUD every launch. Cache it; re-read on the events
    that actually invalidate it.
]]
local SK_VAR  = "aw_spellup_skills_v2"
local REC_VAR = "aw_spellup_recov_v2"

local function save_skills()
    local out = {}
    for id, sk in pairs(skills) do
        table.insert(out, table.concat({ id, sk.name, tonumber(sk.target) or 0,
            tonumber(sk.duration) or 0, tonumber(sk.prac) or 0,
            tonumber(sk.recovery) or -1, tonumber(sk.type) or 0 }, "\t"))
    end
    put_blob(SK_VAR, table.concat(out, "\n"))

    local rec = {}
    for id, name in pairs(recov) do
        table.insert(rec, id .. "\t" .. name)
    end
    put_blob(REC_VAR, table.concat(rec, "\n"))
end

local function load_skills()
    local n = 0

    for _, f in ipairs(rows_of(get_blob(SK_VAR), 7)) do
        local id = tonumber(f[1])
        if id and f[2] ~= "" then
            skills[id] = { name = f[2], target = tonumber(f[3]), duration = tonumber(f[4]),
                           prac = tonumber(f[5]), recovery = tonumber(f[6]),
                           type = tonumber(f[7]) }
            byname[low(f[2])] = id
            n = n + 1
        end
    end

    for _, f in ipairs(rows_of(get_blob(REC_VAR), 2)) do
        local id = tonumber(f[1])
        if id then recov[id] = f[2] end
    end

    return n
end

-- everything we would consider a spellup, by name
local function spellup_ids()
    local out = {}
    for id, s in pairs(skills) do
        if is_spellup(s) then table.insert(out, id) end
    end
    table.sort(out, function(a, b) return skills[a].name < skills[b].name end)
    return out
end

------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- live state
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- seconds left, or nil when it isn't up
local function left(num)
    local t = affect[num]
    if not t then return nil end

    local d = t - now()
    if d <= 0 then affect[num] = nil; return nil end
    return d
end

-- seconds left on this spell's recovery, or nil. One value; see cast_why.
local function recov_left(num)
    local sk = skills[num]
    if type(sk) ~= "table" then return nil end

    local r = tonumber(sk.recovery)
    if not (r and r >= 0) then return nil end

    local t = blocked[r]
    if not t then return nil end

    local d = t - now()
    if d <= 0 then blocked[r] = nil; return nil end
    return d
end

local function recov_label(num)
    local sk = skills[num]
    if type(sk) ~= "table" then return "" end

    local r = tonumber(sk.recovery)
    if not (r and r >= 0) then return "" end
    return recov[r] or ("recovery " .. r)
end

--[[
    One way in, so no path can set an affect and forget to record that the
    spell lasts. That already happened in the Mudlet version: the 'aff' sync
    wrote the expiry directly, the panel filters on hasdur, and a night vision
    with 37 minutes left showed as "nothing running".
]]
local function mark(num, secs)
    num  = tonumber(num)
    secs = tonumber(secs)
    if not num then return end

    if secs and secs > 0 then hasdur[num] = true end
    affect[num] = now() + (secs or 0)
end

--[[
    "5|detect invis~15|detect good" — level and spell name, pairs joined by a
    tilde. Stored as text so what comes back off disk is a string rather than a
    nested table, which is the shape that has caused trouble here before.
]]
local function spells_of(row)
    local out = {}
    if type(row) ~= "table" then return out end

    for _, part in ipairs(split(tostring(row.spells or ""), "~")) do
        if part ~= "" then
            local bits = split(part, "|")
            local lvl  = tonumber(bits[1])
            local name = trim(bits[2] or "")
            if name ~= "" then
                table.insert(out, { level = (lvl and lvl > 0) and lvl or 0, name = name })
            end
        end
    end

    return out
end

local function spells_text(list)
    local out = {}
    for _, sp in ipairs(list) do
        table.insert(out, tostring(sp.level) .. "|" .. sp.name)
    end
    return table.concat(out, "~")
end

-- what a potion grants, as a readable line
local function spells_pretty(row)
    local out = {}

    -- a stored row keeps its spells as text; a box straight off the screen
    -- keeps them as a list, and this is printed for both
    local list = spells_of(row)
    if type(row) == "table" and type(row.spells) == "table" then list = row.spells end

    for _, sp in ipairs(list) do
        table.insert(out, sp.name .. " L" .. sp.level)
    end
    if #out == 0 then return "nothing recorded" end
    return table.concat(out, ", ")
end

local POT_VAR = "aw_spellup_pots_v2"

local function pots_save()
    local out = {}
    for _, r in pairs(pots) do
        --[[
            The count rides along as a seventh field. Rows written before it
            existed have six and still load — rows_of only drops a row that is
            SHORTER than it needs — and an absent count reads as "nobody has
            counted this yet", which is the honest answer for an old row.
        ]]
        local n = count[low(r.keys)]

        table.insert(out, table.concat({ r.keys, r.name, r.where,
            tonumber(r.level) or 0, r.spells, (r.on ~= false) and "1" or "0",
            (type(n) == "number") and n or "" }, "\t"))
    end
    put_blob(POT_VAR, table.concat(out, "\n"))
end

local function pots_load()
    local n = 0
    for _, f in ipairs(rows_of(get_blob(POT_VAR), 6)) do
        if f[1] ~= "" then
            -- NOT "left": that is a file-scope function name, and shadowing
            -- one takes the whole plugin down. See NOTES 9b.
            local have = tonumber(trim(f[7] or ""))
            if have and have >= 0 then count[low(f[1])] = math.floor(have) end

            pots[low(f[1])] = {
                keys   = f[1],
                name   = f[2],
                where  = f[3],
                level  = tonumber(f[4]) or 0,
                spells = f[5],
                on     = (f[6] ~= "0"),
            }
            n = n + 1
        end
    end
    return n
end

-- sorted, so the panel and the help list agree on an order
local function pot_list()
    local out = {}
    for _, r in pairs(pots) do
        if type(r) == "table" then table.insert(out, r) end
    end
    table.sort(out, function(a, b)
        local an = (a.name ~= "" and a.name) or a.keys
        local bn = (b.name ~= "" and b.name) or b.keys
        return low(an) < low(bn)
    end)
    return out
end

local function pot_count()
    local n = 0
    for _ in pairs(pots) do n = n + 1 end
    return n
end

--[[
    Add or merge. Keyed on the keywords, so identifying the same potion twice
    updates the record instead of growing a second one — and a merge keeps the
    fields the new box didn't mention, because an identify without the wish
    comes back partial.
]]
local function pot_put(keys, name, level, spells, where)
    keys = unquote(keys)
    if keys == "" then return nil end

    local k   = low(keys)
    local old = pots[k]

    local row = {
        keys   = keys,
        name   = trim(name or "")  ~= "" and trim(name)  or (old and old.name  or ""),
        where  = trim(where or "") ~= "" and trim(where) or (old and old.where or ""),
        level  = tonumber(level) or (old and old.level) or 0,
        spells = (spells and spells ~= "") and spells or (old and old.spells or ""),
        --[[
            Written as `old and old.on or true`, which is the obvious line and
            is wrong in exactly one case: a row switched OFF gives false, and
            `false or true` is true. So identifying a potion you had
            deliberately disabled turned it back on.
        ]]
        on     = (type(old) == "table") and (old.on ~= false) or true,
    }

    pots[k] = row
    pots_save()
    return row
end

--[[
    REMOVE a key, rather than setting it to nil.

    `t[k] = nil` does not delete the key here — it leaves a null behind that
    pairs() still hands over. Deleting a potion therefore left a null in the
    table and the very next repaint died on it:

        action handler ...: null is not an object (evaluating 'r.keys')
        timer in "Aardwolf Spellups": null is not an object (evaluating 'r.level')

    qpend is the same shape and would have failed silently instead of loudly:
    decide() bails the moment pairs(qpend) yields anything at all, so one
    stale null would have stopped every quaff for the rest of the session with
    nothing on screen to say why.

    Rebuilding without the key is the only version that leaves the table in the
    state the code assumes.
]]
local function forget(t, key)
    local out = {}
    for k, v in pairs(t) do
        if k ~= key and v ~= nil then out[k] = v end
    end
    return out
end

--[[
    Forget what this session decided about a row.

    Deleting a potion left its in-flight entry behind, which blocks every other
    potion for QGRACE seconds, and an out-of-stock mark outlives the restock
    that fixed it.
]]
local function clear_row(k)
    stock   = forget(stock, k)
    qpend   = forget(qpend, k)
end

-- from the protocol doc; see the {sfail} table there
local FAIL = {
    [1]  = { "lost concentration",       "retry" },
    [2]  = { "already affected",         "mark-up" },
    [3]  = { "blocked by a recovery",    "wait-recovery" },
    [4]  = { "not enough mana",          "backoff" },
    [5]  = { "nocast room",              "wait-room" },
    [6]  = { "cannot concentrate",       "retry" },
    [8]  = { "you don't know it",        "never" },
    [9]  = { "self-only cast on other",  "fix-target" },
    [10] = { "resting or sitting",       "stand" },
    [11] = { "disabled",                 "never" },
    [12] = { "not enough moves",         "backoff" },
}

--[[
    Can you cast this yourself?

    Three ways the answer is no, and the MUD is the authority on the last one.
    prac 0 is "in the list for your class but never practised", which reads the
    same as not having it; {sfail} 8 and 11 are the MUD saying so outright and
    they outrank everything.
]]
--[[
    ONE VALUE. NEVER TWO.

    Multiple assignment compiles to destructuring here, and that cuts both
    ways. A function returning two values on one path and one on another dies
    loudly — `action handler ...: true is not iterable`. Padding every path to
    two then breaks the other half SILENTLY: `local ok = can_cast(id)` collects
    the whole pair, and a pair is an object, so it is truthy. Every spell read
    "cast" and the potion path was unreachable; padding recovering() the same
    way put "rec NaN:NaN" beside every buff on the panel.

    So the rule is not "make the paths agree", it is "return one value". A
    reason string, empty when there is no reason. Nothing to destructure,
    nothing to get wrong at a call site, and it reads better anyway.
]]
local function cast_why(num)
    local s = skills[num]
    if type(s) ~= "table"   then return "not in your skill table" end
    if nope[num]            then return "the MUD says you don't know it" end
    if (tonumber(s.prac) or 0) <= 0 then return "unpractised" end
    return ""
end

--[[
    The potion to drink for this buff, or nil.

    Highest SPELL level wins, not highest item level — 'Eyes of Allegiance' is
    a level 4 item that casts level 15 detect good, and a level 40 potion that
    casts level 8 night vision is the worse of the two for night vision. The
    item level is on the panel because it tells you what you are carrying; it
    never decides anything.
]]
--[[
    Usable first, then best.

    Two levels, two jobs. The item's level says whether you may drink it at
    all; the spell's level says how good the buff is. So the item level filters
    and the spell level ranks, and reversing them picks a potion that gives a
    wonderful buff and refuses to go down.

    An unknown character level filters nothing. Guessing "probably too high"
    would silently hide potions that work, and the run cap and the two-strike
    rule already catch the other direction.
]]
local function pot_for(spellName)
    local want = low(spellName)
    local best, bestLvl = nil, -1
    local mine = my_level()

    for _, r in pairs(pots) do
      if type(r) == "table" then
        local usable = (not mine) or (tonumber(r.level) or 0) <= mine

        -- a counted zero is as good a reason to skip as the MUD refusing a get
        if usable and r.on ~= false and stock[low(r.keys)] ~= false
           and count[low(r.keys)] ~= 0 then
            for _, sp in ipairs(spells_of(r)) do
                if low(sp.name) == want and sp.level > bestLvl then
                    best, bestLvl = r, sp.level
                end
            end
        end
      end
    end

    if not best then return nil end
    return { row = best, level = bestLvl }
end

-- every buff any potion in the table can grant, name -> true
local function potion_buffs()
    local out = {}
    for _, r in pairs(pots) do
        if type(r) == "table" then
            for _, sp in ipairs(spells_of(r)) do out[low(sp.name)] = sp.name end
        end
    end
    return out
end


--[[
    Is this buff down and ours to do something about?

    'down' is not 'no affect recorded'. Before a sync there IS no picture, and
    treating that as down is how a fresh login drinks eight potions for eight
    buffs that were all still running. See the sync gate in act().
]]
local function is_down(num)
    return left(num) == nil
end

--[[
    Why the automatic path is holding, or nil if nothing is stopping it.

    Named rather than boolean, because "it isn't doing anything" with no reason
    attached is the single most annoying way for a thing like this to fail. The
    panel prints whatever comes back.
]]
local function held()
    if not cfg.on          then return "switched off" end
    if quiet               then return "stood down — press GO" end
    if not playing()       then return "not in the game yet" end
    if not have_skills()   then return "no skill table — press REFRESH" end
    if not synced          then return "waiting on the first 'aff'" end
    if now() < backoff     then return "backing off (" .. (backoff - now()) .. "s)" end
    if fighting() and not cfg.combat then return "in combat" end
    return nil
end

--[[
    Turn the spellup tags on.

    Core sends 'tags on' and that is NOT enough. Aardwolf's own help is explicit
    that the bare form is a temporary master switch over categories that are
    each enabled separately — "you must enable each category using 'tags
    <tagname> on'" — so with only Core's line sent, {affon} and {affoff} never
    arrive and this entire plugin sits there reporting nothing, with no error
    anywhere to say why.

    'spellups', plural. Confirmed against Aardwolf's own help and unchanged by
    the September 2025 tags rework.

    Sent when you land in the game, and again from anything you pressed
    deliberately. The automatic paths send it once a session — it is a setting
    on your character, not something that needs repeating — but REFRESH forces
    it, because REFRESH is the button you press when this ISN'T working and a
    fix-it button that skips the fix is worse than no button.
]]
local tagsSent = false

local function enable_tags(force)
    if tagsSent and not force then return end
    if not playing() then return end

    tagsSent = true
    send("tags spellups on")
end

--[[
    One command, and it is the MUD's own. It gates on mana, recoveries, nomagic
    rooms, sleeping, combat and affects you already have, which is a longer
    list than anything worth reimplementing out here.
]]
local function fire(manual)
    local why = (not manual) and held()
    if why then return why end
    if manual and not playing() then return "not in the game yet" end

    lastFire = now()
    send("spellup")
    return ""
end

--[[
    get "<keywords>" "<bag>" then quaff "<keywords>".

    Quoted, both of them, because a potion's keywords are a phrase — "potion
    optical precision detectinvis see" — and unquoted that is five arguments.
    Two sends rather than one joined by a separator: there is nothing here to
    ask what the user configured as a command separator, and a hardcoded ';' is
    a guess about whether the MUD splits on it.

    The bag is optional. With none set it assumes the potion is on you, which
    is what a hold-slot potion usually is.
]]
local function quaff(row, why)
    if type(row) ~= "table" then return false end

    local k   = low(row.keys)
    local bag = trim(cfg.bag)

    if bag ~= "" then
        send('get "' .. row.keys .. '" "' .. bag .. '"')
    end
    send('quaff "' .. row.keys .. '"')

    qpend[k]  = now()
    lastQuaff = now()
    run       = run + 1

    utilprint(TAG .. "quaffing " .. ((row.name ~= "" and row.name) or row.keys)
        .. (why and (" — " .. why) or "") .. ".")

    return true
end

-- tags

--[[
    A quaff we sent that the MUD never echoed.

    This used to mean something much stronger — "went down and granted nothing"
    — and switch the potion off after two. That premise was WRONG, and a live
    session disproved it: Shadowbane was switched off as useless, then quaffed
    by hand and granted detect hidden for 7:28. A working potion was being
    struck out because the {affon} this waited on never turned up for it.

    So the signal is the MUD's own "You quaff <thing>." and nothing else. If
    that arrives, the potion went down and this stops watching. If it does not,
    the send did not take — the get was queued behind it, or the potion was not
    where we thought — and all that deserves is to stop waiting so something
    else can go out.

    Nothing switches a row off on its own any more. The run cap is what stops a
    potion that goes down and does nothing, and it stops the whole run rather
    than blaming one row for it.
]]
local function give_up(k)
    qpend = forget(qpend, k)

    local r = pots[k]
    utilprint(TAG .. "$Rno reply to that quaff of "
        .. ((type(r) == "table" and r.name ~= "" and r.name) or k)
        .. " — moving on.$w")
end

local function sweep_pending()
    for k, at in pairs(qpend) do
        if type(at) == "number" and now() - at > QGRACE then give_up(k) end
    end
end

local function on_affon(c, line, w)
    local num  = tonumber(cap(c, w, 1))
    local secs = tonumber(cap(c, w, 2))
    if not num then return end

    mark(num, secs)
    failed[num]  = nil
    dropped[num] = nil

    --[[
        An affect landing means the last potion did its job.
    ]]
    --[[
        An affect landing means the last potion did its job, whatever produced
        it. Only the run counter cares — the wait itself is cleared by the
        MUD's quaff echo, which is the signal that actually arrives.
    ]]
    run     = 0
    retries = 0
end

local function on_affoff(c, line, w)
    local num = tonumber(cap(c, w, 1))
    if not num then return end

    -- something dropped, so "nothing to cast" is no longer true
    castDead = 0

    if affect[num] then dropped[num] = now() end
    affect[num] = nil
end

local function on_sfail(c, line, w)
    local num  = tonumber(cap(c, w, 1))
    local code = tonumber(cap(c, w, 3))
    local rec  = tonumber(cap(c, w, 4))
    if not num then return end

    failed[num] = { code = code, at = now(), recovery = rec }

    -- resting or sitting: firing again just queues the same refusal
    if code == 10 then backoff = now() + 30 end

    --[[
        Queue a retry for the reasons that pass. Code 3 waits on {recoff}
        rather than on a clock, so it parks until that arrives.
    ]]
    local wait = RETRY_IN[code or 0]
    if wait then
        retryAt  = (code == 3) and 0 or (now() + wait)
        retryWhy = (FAIL[code] and FAIL[code][1]) or ("code " .. tostring(code))
    end

    local d = FAIL[code or 0]

    --[[
        8 and 11 mean it is never going to work — you don't know it, or it is
        disabled. That is exactly the case a potion exists for, so it is worth
        saying once rather than leaving it a mystery why casting stopped being
        attempted for that one.
    ]]
    if d and d[2] == "never" then
        if not nope[num] then
            local s = skills[num]
            local nm = (type(s) == "table" and s.name) or tostring(num)
            local p  = pot_for(nm)
            utilprint(TAG .. nm .. ": " .. d[1]
                .. (p and " — there's a potion for it." or " — no potion set for it."))
        end
        nope[num]    = true
        dropped[num] = nil
    end

    -- "already affected" is not a failure, it is the MUD saying our picture is
    -- stale. The 60s is a placeholder until a real {affon} replaces it.
    if code == 2 then mark(num, 60) end
end

local function on_recon(c, line, w)
    local num  = tonumber(cap(c, w, 1))
    local secs = tonumber(cap(c, w, 2))
    if not num then return end
    blocked[num] = now() + (secs or 0)
end

local function on_recoff(c, line, w)
    local num = tonumber(cap(c, w, 1))
    if not num then return end
    blocked[num] = nil

    -- the recovery that was blocking a cast just cleared: that is the cue
    if retryWhy == "blocked by a recovery" then retryAt = now() end
end

local function on_skillgain(c, line, w)
    local num = tonumber(cap(c, w, 1))
    local pct = tonumber(cap(c, w, 2))
    local s   = num and skills[num]
    if type(s) == "table" and pct then s.prac = pct end
end

--[[
    The rows between the markers aren't tagged, so reading them needs a trigger
    that matches a bare row — registered at init and gated, never armed from
    the opening line. A block arrives whole, and a trigger created while that
    packet is being processed does not apply to lines already in it.

    Core classifies spellheaders and recoveries as blocks and gags them. A
    gagged line still reaches every other trigger, so this sees the rows
    regardless of what Core does with them on screen.
]]
local ingest = nil          -- "spells" | "recoveries"
local ingTmr = nil

local render                -- forward: the ingest close repaints
local sync                  -- forward: ...and asks what's running

local function ingest_stop()
    ingest = nil
    if ingTmr then pcall(removeTimer, ingTmr); ingTmr = nil end
end

local function ingest_start(what)
    ingest_stop()
    ingest = what

    ingTmr = addTimer(20000, function()
        if ingest then
            utilprint(TAGR .. "$R{" .. tostring(ingest) .. "} never closed; released.$w")
            ingest_stop()
        end
    end)
end

local function on_spellheaders()
    skills, byname = {}, {}
    ingest_start("spells")
end

local function on_recoveries()
    recov = {}
    ingest_start("recoveries")
end

local function on_ingest_end()
    local what = ingest
    ingest_stop()

    if what == "spells" then
        utilprint(TAG .. skills_count() .. " skills read.")
    elseif what == "recoveries" then
        save_skills()
        if render then render() end
        -- the table is complete; now find out what is already on you
        addTimer(1200, function() if sync then sync() end end)
    end
end

--[[
    skillnum,name,target,duration,prac,recovery,type

    Parsed from both ends rather than by counting commas left to right: the
    name is the only free-text field, so the first field and the last five are
    fixed and everything between them is the name however many commas it has.
]]
local function on_ingest_row(c, line, w)
    if not ingest then return end

    -- the capture, not `line`: the pattern is anchored and the capture is the
    -- whole row, so this is the text the pattern actually agreed to
    local body = cap(c, w, 1)
    if body == "" then body = tostring(line or "") end

    local f = split(body, ",")

    if ingest == "recoveries" then
        -- recnum,name,seconds
        if #f < 3 then return end
        local id = tonumber(trim(f[1]))
        if not id then return end

        local name = {}
        for i = 2, #f - 1 do table.insert(name, f[i]) end
        recov[id] = trim(table.concat(name, ","))
        return
    end

    if #f < 7 then return end

    local id = tonumber(trim(f[1]))
    if not id then return end

    local n    = #f
    local kind = tonumber(trim(f[n]))
    local rec  = tonumber(trim(f[n - 1]))
    local prac = tonumber(trim(f[n - 2]))
    local dur  = tonumber(trim(f[n - 3]))
    local targ = tonumber(trim(f[n - 4]))
    if not (kind and targ) then return end

    local name = {}
    for i = 2, n - 5 do table.insert(name, f[i]) end
    name = trim(table.concat(name, ","))
    if name == "" then return end

    skills[id] = { name = name, target = targ, duration = dur,
                   prac = prac, recovery = rec, type = kind }
    byname[low(name)] = id
end

-- seeding from 'aff'
------------------------------------------------------------------------------

--[[
    {affon} only fires on a fresh cast or quaff. Anything already running when
    you log in is invisible to the tag stream, so the picture starts blank and
    stays wrong until each buff happens to fall and be recast.

    That is not just a cosmetic problem here. A blank picture reads as "eight
    buffs are down" and the automatic path answers that with eight potions. So
    reading 'aff' once is a safety gate, not a nicety: nothing automatic runs
    until it has happened.
]]
--[[
    THE WINDOW IS OPENED BY OUR OWN SEND, NOT BY MATCHING A HEADER.

    The header this used to wait for — "You are affected by the following
    skills/spells:" — is not what Aardwolf prints. The real reply is:

        You have the following special affects:
          No race change               : 1 day and 21:43:21
        You have the following skill/spell modifiers:
          Hammer                       : +3
        You are not affected by any skills or spells.

    So the trigger never fired, the window never opened, and — the part that
    actually mattered — it never CLOSED either. synced stayed false forever and
    held() blocked the whole plugin with "waiting on the first 'aff'", which is
    a plugin that does nothing and cannot say why.

    Opening on our own send fixes the class of bug rather than this instance of
    it. Wording we have not verified can now only cost us the contents of a
    sync; it can no longer wedge the gate shut, because the gate is closed by a
    timer we own.
]]
local syncing = false
local syncN   = 0
local syncTmr = nil
local syncSec = "spells"    -- which section of the reply we are in
local seenNow = {}          -- skillnums this reply actually listed

--[[
    A sync we asked for, whose reply nobody wants to read.

    After a quaff the only honest way to know what landed and for how long is
    to ask — {affon} does not turn up for potions, and a placeholder duration
    is a guess dressed as a fact. So it asks, and hides the answer: gagged from
    "You are affected by the following skills/spells:" through "Use 'saffects'
    ...", inclusive of the blank line in between.

    gagging covers the block once it starts. tailGag carries it past the count
    line to the saffects footer, because the footer's own trigger closes the
    sync and would otherwise let the last two lines through.
]]
local hidden  = false
local gagging = false
local tailGag = false

local function sync_stop()
    syncing = false
    gagging = false
    if syncTmr then pcall(removeTimer, syncTmr); syncTmr = nil end
end

local function sync_done()
    if not syncing then return end
    sync_stop()
    synced = true

    --[[
        'aff' has just listed everything actually up, so every other spellup is
        down — whether or not it has been through an affon/affoff cycle this
        session. Without this, the count of what's down only ever includes
        spells that happened to fall while we were watching, and a fresh login
        sits under the threshold forever with nothing running.
    ]]
    --[[
        'aff' is the WHOLE list, so anything we thought was up and it did not
        mention is not up. Without this the optimistic mark a quaff leaves
        behind would survive a reply that disproved it, and a potion that
        granted nothing would read as working for as long as the guess lasted.
    ]]
    for id in pairs(affect) do
        if not seenNow[id] then affect = forget(affect, id) end
    end

    for _, id in ipairs(spellup_ids()) do
        if not affect[id] and not nope[id] then
            dropped[id] = dropped[id] or now()
        end
    end

    --[[
        A reply that found something running is the picture improving, which is
        the only thing the run cap is really asking about. Without this it only
        ever reset on {affon}, which does not arrive for potions — so a bag of
        potions that all worked perfectly still counted as eight failures in a
        row and stood the whole thing down.
    ]]
    if syncN > 0 then run = 0 end

    -- a hidden sync says nothing; the panel is the output
    if not hidden then
        utilprint(TAG .. "synced — " .. syncN .. " affect(s) already running.")
    end

    hidden = false
    if render then render() end
end

local function sync_open(quiet)
    sync_stop()
    syncing = true
    syncN   = 0
    syncSec = "spells"
    seenNow = {}
    hidden  = (quiet == true)

    -- the backstop, and the only thing that has to work
    syncTmr = addTimer(6000, sync_done)
end

--[[
    Seconds out of whatever Aardwolf put after the colon.

    Four shapes seen or documented: "(00:15)", "(01:02:03)", "21:43:21" bare,
    and "1 day and 21:43:21". Rather than a pattern per shape, take the LAST
    clock in the text and add the days if a number precedes the word "day" —
    which covers all four and anything else of the same family.

    "+3" has no clock in it and falls out as nil, which is right: a skill
    modifier is not an affect and must not be marked as one.
]]
local function read_clock(text)
    text = tostring(text or "")

    local best, i = nil, 1
    while i <= string.len(text) do
        local ch = string.sub(text, i, i)
        if ch >= "0" and ch <= "9" then
            local j, part = i, ""
            while j <= string.len(text) do
                local c2 = string.sub(text, j, j)
                if (c2 >= "0" and c2 <= "9") or c2 == ":" then
                    part = part .. c2
                    j = j + 1
                else
                    break
                end
            end

            if string.find(part, ":", 1, true) then
                local bits = split(part, ":")
                local n = #bits
                local h, m, sec
                if n >= 3 then
                    h, m, sec = tonumber(bits[n - 2]), tonumber(bits[n - 1]), tonumber(bits[n])
                else
                    h, m, sec = 0, tonumber(bits[1]), tonumber(bits[2])
                end
                if h and m and sec then best = h * 3600 + m * 60 + sec end
            end
            i = j
        else
            i = i + 1
        end
    end

    if not best then return nil end

    -- "1 day and 21:43:21"
    local at = string.find(low(text), "day", 1, true)
    if at then
        --[[
            The LAST digit run before the word, kept rather than accumulated.
            Written as a single running string it cleared itself on the space
            in "1 day" and came back empty, so the day was silently dropped and
            a 45-hour affect read as 21 hours.
        ]]
        local head, last, cur = string.sub(text, 1, at - 1), "", ""
        for k = 1, string.len(head) do
            local c3 = string.sub(head, k, k)
            if c3 >= "0" and c3 <= "9" then
                cur = cur .. c3
            else
                if cur ~= "" then last = cur end
                cur = ""
            end
        end
        if cur ~= "" then last = cur end

        local days = tonumber(last)
        if days and days > 0 then best = best + days * 86400 end
    end

    return best
end

--[[
    Every potion in the table can come off an identify box, because the box
    carries all four things this needs and nothing else does:

        | Keywords   : potion optical precision detectinvis see           |
        | Name       : [Potion] Optical Precision                         |
        | Type       : Potion                    Level  :     5           |
        | Spells     : 1 use of level 5 'detect invis'                    |

    Keywords and Spells both wrap onto unlabelled rows, so a continuation goes
    onto whichever of them was last open — that is how the second half of a
    long keyword string, and the second spell of a two-spell potion, get in.

    Nothing here sends anything. It reads boxes that already scrolled past,
    which means identifying a potion for any other reason quietly fills this in
    as a side effect.
]]
local box     = nil       -- the record being built
local boxLast = nil       -- which repeating field a bare ": ..." row continues
local seen    = nil       -- the last potion identified, offered on the panel
--[[
    Every potion identified this session, by keywords, so the "keep it" link
    printed under each box still works after three more have scrolled past.
]]
local seenBox = {}

--[[
    What the box reader actually saw, kept whether or not it produced a potion.

    A capture that silently does nothing is the worst thing to debug from a
    screenshot: the box scrolls past looking perfect and the panel says "no
    potions yet", and every stage between those two is invisible. So each stage
    leaves a mark and 'awbuff raw' prints them. Three counters and a reason
    turn "it didn't work" into "the start line never matched", which is an
    answer rather than a place to start guessing.
]]
local dbg = { start = 0, rows = 0, ends = 0, last = "nothing yet", why = "" }

--[[
    "1 use of level 5 'detect invis'" — scanned character by character.

    No string.find, and that is the whole point. The first version of this box
    reader was built on string.find and Lua patterns, and the offsets came back
    wrong: EVERY row of the box was mistaken for an unlabelled continuation of
    the Keywords field, so `keys` ended up holding the entire box, Type was
    never read, and every potion was rejected as "not a potion". Nine boxes,
    124 rows, nothing captured.

    A scan has no offset convention to disagree about. Note also that
    string.find's `init` argument does not advance the search on this runtime
    (MUDFORGE-NOTES #11), so the "find the next quote from here" shape this
    used to have was unreliable even where the first offset was right.

    The level here is the SPELL's, which is the number the whole choice turns
    on, and it is not the item's level on the row above.
]]
local function read_spell(text)
    text = tostring(text or "")
    local n = string.len(text)

    local i, lvl = 1, nil
    while i <= n do
        if string.sub(text, i, i + 5) == "level " then
            local j, digits = i + 6, ""
            while j <= n do
                local ch = string.sub(text, j, j)
                if ch >= "0" and ch <= "9" then
                    digits = digits .. ch
                    j = j + 1
                else
                    break
                end
            end

            local v = tonumber(digits)
            if v then lvl = v; i = j; break end
        end
        i = i + 1
    end

    if not lvl then return nil end

    -- the name lives between the next pair of single quotes
    local q1 = nil
    while i <= n do
        if string.sub(text, i, i) == "'" then q1 = i; break end
        i = i + 1
    end
    if not q1 then return nil end

    local name = ""
    i = q1 + 1
    while i <= n do
        local ch = string.sub(text, i, i)
        if ch == "'" then
            name = trim(name)
            if name == "" then return nil end
            return { level = lvl, name = name }
        end
        name = name .. ch
        i = i + 1
    end

    return nil
end

local function box_store()
    local b = box
    box, boxLast = nil, nil

    if type(b) ~= "table" then return end

    dbg.last = "kind=" .. tostring(b.kind) .. "  keys=" .. tostring(b.keys)
        .. "  name=" .. tostring(b.name) .. "  L" .. tostring(b.level)
        .. "  spells=" .. tostring(#b.spells)

    if low(tostring(b.kind)) ~= "potion" then
        dbg.why = "not a potion — Type read as '" .. tostring(b.kind) .. "'"
        return
    end
    if trim(tostring(b.keys)) == "" then
        dbg.why = "no keywords came out of the box"
        return
    end
    if #b.spells == 0 then
        dbg.why = "no Spells line — nothing for it to cast"
        return
    end

    dbg.why = "kept"
    seen = b

    --[[
        Seen, not kept. It asks.

        Auto-adding was the obvious way to remove the typing and it is the
        wrong trade for this plugin: a row in the table is a thing that may one
        day be drunk, and a plugin that quietly decides what it is allowed to
        drink is a plugin you have to audit. Ask, and make saying yes cost one
        click instead of a typed command.

        Every box gets its own link, keyed by its own keywords, so identifying
        three potions in a row leaves three offers rather than one that only
        remembers the last.
    ]]
    seenBox[low(b.keys)] = b

    local shown = (b.name ~= "" and b.name) or b.keys

    if pots[low(b.keys)] then
        -- already ours: the box is fresher, so take its spells and level
        pot_put(b.keys, b.name, b.level, spells_text(b.spells), b.where)
        utilprint(TAG .. "updated " .. shown .. " — "
            .. spells_pretty(pots[low(b.keys)]) .. ".")
    else
        utilprint(TAG .. "potion: " .. shown .. " — " .. spells_pretty(b) .. ".")

        if type(hyperlink) == "function" then
            pcall(hyperlink, "$G  [keep it]$w   $K(adds it to the potion table)$w",
                  'awbuff add "' .. b.keys .. '"',
                  { hint = "add " .. shown .. " to the potion table" })
        else
            utilprint("$K  'awbuff add' to keep it.$w")
        end
    end

    if render then render() end
end

local function on_box_start(c, line, w)
    dbg.start = dbg.start + 1
    dbg.why   = "box open, never closed"

    box = { keys = trim(cap(c, w, 1)), name = "", kind = "", where = "",
            level = 0, spells = {} }
    boxLast = "keys"
end


--[[
    One trigger per field, instead of one trigger and a hand-written parser.

    The trigger engine is JavaScript regex and it demonstrably works — every
    tag in this plugin goes through it. The parser underneath did not. So the
    splitting happens where it is reliable, and what arrives here is already a
    label and a value.

    The Type row carries two pairs — "Type : Potion    Level : 5" — so its
    pattern takes both, with the level group LAST because an optional group
    anywhere else poisons cap()'s index-base inference (NOTES #14).
]]
local function on_box_name(c, line, w)
    if not box then return end
    dbg.rows = dbg.rows + 1
    -- stripped of the (!( )!) colour markers, so it matches the same item
    -- sitting in the bag when a listing goes past
    box.name = clean_name(cap(c, w, 1))
    boxLast  = nil
end

local function on_box_type(c, line, w)
    if not box then return end
    dbg.rows = dbg.rows + 1

    box.kind = trim(cap(c, w, 1))

    local lvl = trim(cap(c, w, 2))
    if lvl ~= "" then box.level = tonumber(lvl) or box.level end

    boxLast = nil
end

local function on_box_spells(c, line, w)
    if not box then return end
    dbg.rows = dbg.rows + 1

    local sp = read_spell(cap(c, w, 1))
    if sp then table.insert(box.spells, sp) end

    boxLast = "spells"
end

--[[
    An unlabelled "  : more text" row, which continues whichever repeating
    field was last open. Both of the fields that wrap matter: half a keyword
    string is a 'get' that fails, and a missing second spell is a potion that
    never gets picked for the buff it grants.
]]
local function on_box_more(c, line, w)
    if not box then return end
    dbg.rows = dbg.rows + 1

    local rest = trim(cap(c, w, 1))
    if rest == "" then return end

    if boxLast == "keys" then
        box.keys = trim(box.keys .. " " .. rest)
    elseif boxLast == "spells" then
        local sp = read_spell(rest)
        if sp then table.insert(box.spells, sp) end
    end
end

local function on_box_end()
    if not box then return end
    dbg.ends = dbg.ends + 1
    box_store()
end

-- can you drink it at all? nil level means we do not know, so we do not judge
local function too_high(row)
    local mine = my_level()
    if not mine then return false end
    return (tonumber(row.level) or 0) > mine
end

local function count_text(row)
    local n = count[low(row.keys)]
    if type(n) ~= "number" then return "?" end
    if n <= 0 then return "none" end
    return tostring(n)
end

local function set_count(k, n)
    if type(n) ~= "number" then return end
    if n < 0 then n = 0 end

    count[k] = n
    pots_save()

    local r = pots[k]
    local nm = (type(r) == "table" and r.name ~= "" and r.name) or k

    --[[
        Said once per potion per time it crosses the line, not once per quaff.
        Reset when it goes back above, so restocking re-arms it — otherwise the
        first shopping trip of the session buys you silence for the rest of it.

        A threshold of 0 turns it off. That is a real setting rather than an
        edge case: plenty of people know perfectly well what is in the bag.
    ]]
    if cfg.low <= 0 then return end

    if n > cfg.low then
        lowSaid[k] = nil
    elseif not lowSaid[k] then
        lowSaid[k] = true

        --[[
            Deliberately three lines with a rule under them. A single red
            sentence in the middle of combat spam is a sentence you do not
            read, and the entire point of this is that you find out before the
            bag is empty rather than after.
        ]]
        utilprint("$R" .. string.rep("-", 52) .. "$w")
        utilprint(TAG .. "$R" .. (n <= 0 and "OUT OF" or ("DOWN TO " .. n))
            .. " " .. string.upper(nm) .. "$w")
        utilprint("$w  " .. (n <= 0 and "None" or tostring(n)) .. " left"
            .. (trim(cfg.bag) ~= "" and (" in the " .. cfg.bag) or "")
            .. (type(r) == "table" and r.where ~= "" and (" — bought at " .. r.where) or "")
            .. ". Time to buy more.")
        utilprint("$R" .. string.rep("-", 52) .. "$w")
    end
end

-- everything at or under the warning line, for the panel's banner
local function low_rows()
    local out = {}
    if cfg.low <= 0 then return out end

    for k, r in pairs(pots) do
        local n = count[k]
        if type(r) == "table" and r.on ~= false and type(n) == "number" and n <= cfg.low then
            table.insert(out, { row = r, n = n })
        end
    end

    table.sort(out, function(a, b) return a.n < b.n end)
    return out
end

--[[
    Which of our potions a listed line is.

    Matched on the short description, because that is what a container listing
    prints — the keywords never appear in it. So a potion counts only once its
    name is known, which in practice means once it has been identified. A row
    typed in by hand with no name is honest about that: the panel shows "?"
    rather than a number it never had.
]]
--[[
    LONGEST match wins, not the first one pairs() happens to hand over.

    Carry "Green Tea" and "Green Tea Supreme" and both names are inside the
    Supreme's listing row — so the first hit is whichever order the table
    iterated in, which is arbitrary and can differ between two runs. The count
    then lands on the wrong potion, silently, and nothing about the number
    looks wrong.

    Matched on the plain text, markers and all, because both sources use the
    same convention: the identify box says "(!(Shadowbane)!)" and so does the
    bag listing. Storing the ANSI instead would mean exact-matching escape
    sequences generated in two different contexts — a box row and a listing row
    with (Glow) (Hum) and a count in front of it — for no extra information,
    and it would fail the same silent way when they differed.
]]
local function row_in_line(text)
    text = low(text)

    local best, bestLen = nil, 0
    for k, r in pairs(pots) do
        local nm = (type(r) == "table") and low(clean_name(r.name)) or ""
        if nm ~= "" and string.len(nm) > bestLen and contains(text, nm) then
            best, bestLen = k, string.len(nm)
        end
    end
    return best
end

--[[
    A container listing going past, which is where the numbers come from.

    Only OUR bag: inventory and every other container use the same shape, and
    taking numbers off the wrong one would say you have two sanctuary potions
    while ninety sit in the potion bag.
]]
--[[
    Is this listing OUR bag?

    The header prints the container's NAME — "The Satchel of Sanctity
    contains:" — and the bag is set by KEYWORDS, "satchel sanctity
    crusaderbag", because that is what 'get' needs. Testing one as a substring
    of the other can never match, so COUNT THE BAG sent its command, the MUD
    answered with the whole listing, and every potion stayed at "? left".

    So: any keyword of three letters or more turning up in the header. One is
    enough — you chose these words to name this container — and short ones are
    skipped because "of" and "a" match everything.
]]
local function bag_header(name)
    local bag = trim(cfg.bag)
    if bag == "" then return false end

    name = low(name)

    for _, word in ipairs(argv(low(bag))) do
        if string.len(word) >= 3 and string.find(name, word, 1, true) then
            return true
        end
    end
    return false
end

local function on_bag_start(c, line, w)
    if trim(cfg.bag) == "" then return end

    if not bag_header(cap(c, w, 1)) then
        inBag = false
        return
    end

    inBag, bagSaw = true, {}

    -- the listing arrives in one packet, so a short timer closes it
    if bagTmr then pcall(removeTimer, bagTmr) end
    bagTmr = addTimer(1500, function()
        if inBag then
            --[[
                Anything of ours that did NOT appear in a listing of the bag is
                not in the bag. That is worth knowing before the first failed
                get rather than after it.
            ]]
            for k in pairs(pots) do
                if not bagSaw[k] then set_count(k, 0) end
            end
            render()
        end
        inBag, bagTmr = false, nil
    end)
end

local function saw_in_bag(text, n)
    if type(stripAnsiCodes) == "function" then
        local ok, clean = pcall(stripAnsiCodes, text)
        if ok and type(clean) == "string" then text = clean end
    end

    local k = row_in_line(text)
    if not k then return end

    bagSaw[k] = true
    set_count(k, n)
end

--[[
    A counted row of the listing:  (  3)     a potion of sanctuary
]]
local function on_bag_line(c, line, w)
    if not inBag then return end
    saw_in_bag(cap(c, w, 2), tonumber(cap(c, w, 1)) or 1)
end

--[[
    ...and an uncounted one, which is how a single potion is printed. One is
    one; there is no number on the line to read.
]]
local function on_bag_single(c, line, w)
    if not inBag then return end
    saw_in_bag(cap(c, w, 1), 1)
end

--[[
    'You quaff <thing>.' — one actually went down.

    The MUD's own echo rather than our send, because a send can fail: the get
    was queued behind it, or you weren't holding one. And it counts a potion
    you drank by hand, which comes out of the same bag.
]]
--[[
    Go and find out what is actually running, quietly.

    One 'aff', the reply gagged, and the panel simply updates. Debounced,
    because a run of quaffs — or a spellup that queues six spells — should cost
    one of these rather than one each.

    Both paths need it. Only the quaff path had it, so a buff that 'spellup'
    recast never came back to the panel: the MUD said "Queueing spell :
    underwater breathing", then "You feel gills growing on your neck!", and
    the row stayed gone because nothing ever asked.
]]
--[[
    Longer after a cast than after a quaff. 'spellup' QUEUES — "Queueing spell
    : underwater breathing." — and works through them a couple of seconds
    apart, so asking after five would catch the first and miss the rest.

    A local rather than another file-scope constant: this file is at Lua's
    limit of 200 of those, and one more does not compile.
]]
local function resync(cast)
    if now() - lastAff <= 8 then return end

    local wait = cast and 12000 or POT_AFF_WAIT

    lastAff = now()
    addTimer(wait, function()
        if playing() and have_skills() then
            sync_open(true)
            send("aff")
        end
    end)
end

local function on_quaff(c, line, w)
    local what = cap(c, w, 1)

    if type(stripAnsiCodes) == "function" then
        local ok, clean = pcall(stripAnsiCodes, what)
        if ok and type(clean) == "string" then what = clean end
    end

    local k = row_in_line(what)

    --[[
        Nothing matched by name, but we have a quaff in flight — so it is that
        one. This is the path a hand-typed row with no name takes, and without
        it those never count down at all.
    ]]
    if not k then
        for key, at in pairs(qpend) do
            if now() - at <= 5 then k = key end
        end
    end

    if not k then return end

    -- it went down: stop waiting on it, and take one off the count
    qpend = forget(qpend, k)
    stock = forget(stock, k)

    if type(count[k]) == "number" then set_count(k, count[k] - 1) end

    --[[
        ONE echo, one consumption, and every spell on that potion is now on you.

            You quaff (!(Eyes of Allegiance)!).
            Your eyes glow yellow.      <- detect good
            Your eyes glow red.         <- detect evil

        Marked optimistically, because waiting for {affon} to say so does not
        work: a potion that demonstrably granted detect hidden for 7:28 never
        produced one. Without this the buff stays "down" the instant after it
        landed and the next tick quaffs another, and another, until the run cap
        or the bag runs out.

        PLACEHOLDER seconds, and deliberately not a guess dressed up as a fact:
        the next 'aff' replaces it with the real clock. Erring long costs a
        little downtime; erring short costs potions, and potions are the thing
        this is careful with.
    ]]
    local r = pots[k]
    if type(r) ~= "table" then return end

    --[[
        A short optimistic mark, only to bridge the couple of seconds until the
        hidden 'aff' comes back with the real clocks. Long enough that the next
        tick does not quaff a second one; short enough that if the potion
        granted nothing, and the reply says so, nothing is left believing it —
        and sync_done drops anything the reply did not list anyway.
    ]]
    for _, sp in ipairs(spells_of(r)) do
        local id = byname[low(sp.name)]
        if id then mark(id, POT_GUESS) end
    end

    --[[
        ...and go and find out for real, once, a beat later. One command, and
        it is the difference between a placeholder that decays into a wrong
        answer and one that gets corrected.
    ]]
    --[[
        ...then ask for the truth, quietly — see resync().
    ]]
    resync(false)
end
