--[[
    How many buffs 'spellup' would actually cast right now.

    CASTABLE ones. This counted every spellup in the table, and the table is
    the whole game's 619 skills rather than your own — so it reported "151
    down", sent 'spellup' on the strength of it, and the MUD answered "No
    spells or skills cast." every time, because 151 of those are spells this
    character has never had.

    Counting what the MUD would act on makes the number mean something and
    makes the threshold mean something with it.
]]
local function downcount()
    local n = 0
    for id in pairs(dropped) do
        if is_spellup(skills[id]) and not nope[id] and is_down(id)
           and cast_why(id) == "" then
            n = n + 1
        end
    end
    return n
end

--[[
    The buff that most wants a potion, or nil.

    Only buffs that are down, that a potion in OUR table grants, and that we
    have concluded we cannot cast. Highest spell level available breaks the
    tie, so the potion you'd have picked by hand is the one that goes.
]]
--[[
    WHAT TO REACH FOR WHEN YOU COULD DO EITHER.

    "cast"  — if you know the spell, cast it, even when a potion would land a
              stronger version. Potions are only for buffs you cannot cast at
              all, and then it drinks the highest-level one you can use.

    "level" — take whichever lands the better buff. A cast lands at YOUR level,
              so at 11 a level 15 potion beats casting detect good yourself;
              once you outlevel the potion, casting wins again.

    The ordering matters and only in "level" mode. A potion that beats your
    cast has to go down BEFORE 'spellup', because the MUD casts everything it
    can the moment that command lands — the buff would be up, at the weaker
    level, and the potion would never get its turn. decide() flips the order
    for exactly that reason.

    Neither mode can stop the MUD casting something. 'spellup' is one command
    and it picks the whole list itself; 'forgetskill' is Aardwolf's own way to
    take a spell out of it, and it does that properly.
]]
local function next_potion()
    local best, bestRow, bestLvl, bestWhy = nil, nil, -1, nil
    local mine = my_level()

    for _, name in pairs(potion_buffs()) do
        local id = byname[low(name)]
        if id and is_down(id) then
            local why = cast_why(id)
            local p   = pot_for(name)

            --[[
                Castable, but the potion is stronger. Only "level" mode cares,
                and only when we know what level the cast would land at — with
                no character level there is nothing to compare and casting is
                the free option, so it stays the answer.
            ]]
            if why == "" and cfg.prefer == "level" and p and mine
               and p.level > mine then
                why = "L" .. p.level .. " beats casting it at " .. mine
            end

            if why ~= "" and p and not qpend[low(p.row.keys)] and p.level > bestLvl then
                best, bestRow, bestLvl, bestWhy = name, p.row, p.level, why
            end
        end
    end

    if not bestRow then return nil end
    return { row = bestRow, why = best .. " is down, " .. bestWhy }
end

--[[
    One pass. Casting first, because the MUD's spellup is free of the two
    things that make potions worth rationing — it costs mana rather than an
    item, and it cannot go down and grant nothing.
]]
--[[
    What the button does: one full pass, right now.

    It only ever sent 'spellup', which is why pressing it never drank anything
    — a fair thing to expect of the button whose whole job is "do it now".

    The pacing gates do not apply: you asked. The SYNC gate still does, because
    without it there is no picture of what is already running and "do it now"
    would drink a potion for a buff with twenty minutes left on it.

    One potion per press. A button that empties eight potions into the queue
    because you pressed it once is not a button anybody wants twice.
]]
local function run_now()
    if not playing() then
        utilprint(TAG .. "$Rnot in the game yet.$w")
        return
    end

    local function cast_it()
        if fire(true) ~= "" then return false end
        utilprint(TAG .. "sent 'spellup'.")
        resync(true)
        return true
    end

    local function quaff_it()
        if not cfg.potions then return false end
        if not synced then return false end

        local pick = next_potion()
        if not pick then return false end

        quaff(pick.row, pick.why)
        return true
    end

    local cast, drank
    if cfg.prefer == "level" then
        drank = quaff_it()
        cast  = cast_it()
    else
        cast  = cast_it()
        drank = quaff_it()
    end

    if not synced then
        utilprint(TAG .. "$Rnot synced, so nothing was quaffed — press SYNC.$w")
    elseif not (cast or drank) then
        utilprint(TAG .. "nothing to do: everything is either up or has no potion.")
    end
end

local function decide()
    sweep_pending()

    if held() then return end

    -- something is already in flight; nothing else goes out behind it
    for _ in pairs(qpend) do return end

    if run >= cfg.cap then
        quiet = true
        utilprint(TAG .. "$R" .. run .. " potions in a row without the picture "
            .. "improving — standing down. 'awbuff go' to start it again.$w")
        if render then render() end
        return
    end

    --[[
        A queued retry jumps the cast cooldown, because the cooldown is pacing
        for a routine top-up and this is a cast the MUD already refused once
        for a reason that has since cleared. It does not jump RETRY_GAP, and it
        does not get to run forever: a reason that never clears would re-send
        every few seconds for the rest of the session.
    ]]
    local function retry_pass()
        if retryAt <= 0 or now() < retryAt then return false end
        if retries >= RETRY_MAX then return false end
        if (now() - lastFire) < RETRY_GAP then return false end

        -- no clock fixes sitting down, or casting mid-fight
        if retryWhy == "resting or sitting" and state() ~= 3 then return false end
        if retryWhy == "cannot concentrate" and fighting() then return false end

        if fire(false) ~= "" then return false end

        retryAt  = 0
        retries  = retries + 1
        utilprint(TAG .. "retrying after " .. retryWhy .. ".")
        return true
    end

    local function cast_pass()
        if retry_pass() then return true end

        --[[
            Only casting waits this out. held() would have been the tidy place
            to put it and would have been wrong: it gates the potion half too,
            and "the MUD had nothing to cast" is not a reason to stop drinking
            a potion for a buff it cannot cast in the first place.
        ]]
        if now() < castDead then return false end

        if downcount() < cfg.threshold then return false end
        if (now() - lastFire) < cfg.cooldown then return false end
        if fire(false) ~= "" then return false end

        utilprint(TAG .. downcount() .. " buff(s) down — sent 'spellup'.")
        resync(true)
        return true
    end

    local function quaff_pass()
        --[[
            The switch that spends things, kept separate from the one that
            casts. Casting costs mana and mana comes back; a potion is gone.
            Plenty of nights you want the buffs kept up and the bag left alone,
            and until now the only way to say that was to turn the whole plugin
            off.

            Clicking a buff still works — that is you deciding, once.
        ]]
        if not cfg.potions then return false end

        if (now() - lastQuaff) < cfg.gap then return false end

        local pick = next_potion()
        if not pick then return false end

        quaff(pick.row, pick.why)
        return true
    end

    --[[
        Order is the whole of the setting. In "level" mode a potion that beats
        your cast has to land BEFORE 'spellup' goes out, or the MUD casts the
        weaker version, the buff is up, and the potion never gets its turn.
    ]]
    if cfg.prefer == "level" then
        if quaff_pass() then return end
        cast_pass()
    else
        if cast_pass() then return end
        quaff_pass()
    end
end

                .. " — skipping it.$w")

--[[
    Get the picture straight the moment you're actually in the game.

    Everything this plugin knows starts wrong: the skill table may be cached
    from a previous class, and {affon} only fires on a fresh cast, so whatever
    is already running when you log in is invisible until it falls off. Both
    have a fix that is one command each, and there is no reason to make you
    press a button for something that has to happen every single session.

    STATE 3, not "char.status arrived". This is the one thing to get right
    here, and the Mudlet version got it wrong first: Aardwolf sends char.status
    during the LOGIN SEQUENCE with state 1 and 2, so latching on the packet set
    the flag at the name prompt and sent 'slist spells' three seconds later —
    into the password field, which echoes nothing. The login just failed, with
    no sign anywhere of why.

    playing() is state >= 3, which is the first moment a command goes to the
    game rather than to a prompt.
]]
local greeted = false

local function on_status()
    --[[
        Back at a prompt: re-arm, and drop what we thought we knew.

        dropped in particular. It is the running total of what owes a recast,
        and carrying it across a reconnect means that the instant you are back
        in, before 'aff' has re-synced anything, the automatic path fires off
        whatever debt was outstanding when you dropped.
    ]]
    if not playing() then
        greeted, synced = false, false
        dropped = {}
        return
    end

    if greeted then return end
    greeted = true

    if not cfg.login then return end

    --[[
        A beat after landing rather than on the packet. The login sequence is
        still printing, Core is still rebuilding its supports, and a command
        sent into the middle of that is a command in the middle of the MOTD.
    ]]
    addTimer(1500, function()
        if not playing() then return end
        enable_tags()

        if not have_skills() then
            utilprint(TAG .. "reading the skill table...")
            send("slist spells")     -- the ingest chains into a sync when it closes
        else
            sync()
        end
    end)
end

local LIMITS = {
    threshold = { lo = 1, hi = 40, step = 1, label = "cast at",
                  unit = " down", note = "spellups down before 'spellup' goes out" },
    cooldown  = { lo = 5, hi = 600, step = 5, label = "cast gap",
                  unit = "s", note = "minimum between 'spellup' sends" },
    gap       = { lo = 1, hi = 60, step = 1, label = "potion gap",
                  unit = "s", note = "minimum between potions" },
    cap       = { lo = 1, hi = 50, step = 1, label = "run cap",
                  unit = "", note = "potions in a row, then it stands down" },
    low       = { lo = 0, hi = 50, step = 1, label = "warn at",
                  unit = " left", note = "tell you to buy more; 0 never does" },
}

local function clamp(key, n)
    local L = LIMITS[key]
    if not L then return n end
    if n < L.lo then return L.lo end
    if n > L.hi then return L.hi end
    return n
end

local function stepper(key)
    local L = LIMITS[key]
    return '<div class="row">'
        .. '<span class="lb">' .. L.label .. '</span>'
        .. '<div class="stp" data-mud-action="dec" data-mud-data="' .. key .. '">−</div>'
        .. '<span class="val">' .. cfg[key] .. L.unit .. '</span>'
        .. '<div class="stp" data-mud-action="inc" data-mud-data="' .. key .. '">+</div>'
        .. '<span class="note">' .. L.note .. '</span>'
        .. '</div>'
end

--[[
    What the buffs view lists.

    Everything running, plus every buff a potion in the table can grant even
    when it has never been seen — a row you added for sanctuary is worth
    showing as "down, potion ready" before the first time it drops, because
    that is when you want to know it's wired up correctly.
]]
--[[
    EVERY FIELD IS SET ON EVERY ROW, and none of them is nil.

    `{ id = id, name = n, left = d }` does not create a `left` key when d is
    nil, and reading a key that was never created gives JavaScript `undefined`
    — which is neither nil nor false, so `if r.unknown then` is TRUE on a row
    that never had an `unknown` field. Three buffs read straight off 'aff',
    with live countdowns beside them, were all labelled "no such spell".

    Real Lua cannot reproduce this: a missing key is nil there, so the sim runs
    green over it forever. The only defence is to never let the shape of a row
    vary — `false` and `0` instead of absent, and `== true` instead of
    truthiness on anything read back out.
]]
local function buff_rows()
    local out, seenId = {}, {}

    for id in pairs(affect) do
        local d = left(id)
        if d and skills[id] and hasdur[id] then
            table.insert(out, { id = id, name = skills[id].name,
                                secs = d, up = true, unknown = false })
            seenId[id] = true
        end
    end

    --[[
        A spell you can CAST stays on the list when it drops.

        It used to leave with its timer. The panel emptied to two rows while
        six buffs were plainly castable and plainly down — which reads as
        nothing to do, when in fact everything on it needed doing. A row that
        vanishes cannot be clicked to put itself back either.

        Off `dropped` — the ones that have actually been up and fallen off —
        rather than every spellup spell you know. LEAVE it in, not put the
        whole spellbook in: a level 200 skill table has hundreds of castable
        self-buffs and no one wants a panel listing all of them, most of which
        were never part of the rotation.

        Same test the automatic path uses to decide whether 'spellup' is worth
        sending, so the list and the decision agree: a self-targeting spellup
        skill, not one switched off, and castable right now.
    ]]
    for id in pairs(dropped) do
        local sk = skills[id]
        if sk and not seenId[id] and is_spellup(sk) and not nope[id]
           and cast_why(id) == "" then
            table.insert(out, { id = id, name = sk.name,
                                secs = 0, up = false, unknown = false })
            seenId[id] = true
        end
    end

    for _, name in pairs(potion_buffs()) do
        local id = byname[low(name)]
        if id and not seenId[id] then
            table.insert(out, { id = id, name = name,
                                secs = 0, up = false, unknown = false })
            seenId[id] = true
        elseif not id and not seenId["n:" .. low(name)] then
            table.insert(out, { id = false, name = name,
                                secs = 0, up = false, unknown = true })
            seenId["n:" .. low(name)] = true
        end
    end

    table.sort(out, function(a, b)
        if (a.up == true) ~= (b.up == true) then return a.up == true end
        if a.up == true and b.up == true then return a.secs < b.secs end
        return low(a.name) < low(b.name)
    end)

    return out
end

-- how this buff is going to get put back on, in three words
--[[
    What the panel says has to be what decide() would actually do.

    This used to answer "cast" for anything castable, full stop — so in
    "strongest effect" mode it drank the potion and went on displaying "cast"
    beside it. A panel that disagrees with the plugin is worse than no panel,
    because it is the thing you check when you are trying to work out what the
    plugin is doing. Same rule as next_potion, deliberately in step with it.
]]
local function source_of(r)
    if r.unknown == true then return { text = "no such spell", cls = "bad" } end

    local p = pot_for(r.name)

    if cast_why(r.id) == "" then
        local mine = my_level()
        if cfg.prefer == "level" and p and mine and p.level > mine then
            return { text = "potion L" .. p.level, cls = "pot" }
        end
        return { text = "cast", cls = "cast" }
    end

    if p then return { text = "potion L" .. p.level, cls = "pot" } end

    return { text = "no potion set", cls = "bad" }
end

local function timer_text(r)
    if r.up == true then return fmt(r.secs) end
    if r.unknown == true then return "-" end

    local d = recov_left(r.id)
    if d then return "rec " .. fmt(d) end

    return "down"
end

-- the key a row's countdown is bound to, same on both sides of the repaint
local function bind_key(r)
    if r.unknown == true then return "t" .. low(r.name) end
    return "t" .. tostring(r.id)
end

--[[
    Countdowns go through bound values, not a repaint.

    The panel ticks every second to keep the clocks honest. Rebuilding it that
    often throws away whatever is half typed in the add-potion box, which is
    the one thing on here that can't be redone in a click, and it resets the
    scroll on a table that gets long.

    So the full render only happens when the SHAPE changes — a buff appearing
    or falling, a row switching source — and the rest of the time this pushes
    text into the spans that already exist.
]]
local shape = nil

local function shape_of(rows)
    local out = {}
    for _, r in ipairs(rows) do
        -- named, not '_': the loop already binds '_' in this scope and the
        -- transpiler emits `let`, which cannot be declared twice. That fails
        -- the ENTIRE plugin load, not this function.
        local src = source_of(r)
        table.insert(out, bind_key(r) .. ":" .. ((r.up == true) and "u" or "d")
            .. src.cls .. src.text)
    end

    --[[
        The low banner is part of the shape, not part of the clock. Left out of
        this, it would only appear on the next repaint something else happened
        to force — so the potion you just drank your last of stays unremarked
        until you click something.
    ]]
    for _, e in ipairs(low_rows()) do
        table.insert(out, "low:" .. low(e.row.keys) .. "=" .. e.n)
    end

    table.insert(out, "auto:" .. tostring(cfg.on))

    return table.concat(out, ",")
end

local function tick_panel()
    if not widget then return end

    local rows = buff_rows()
    local sig  = shape_of(rows)

    if sig ~= shape then
        shape = sig
        if render then render() end
        return
    end

    for _, r in ipairs(rows) do
        pcall(setBoundValue, widget, bind_key(r), timer_text(r))
    end

    -- same rule as the header: a reason only when auto is on and something
    -- other than the switch is stopping it
    local hold = held()
    pcall(setBoundValue, widget, "state", (cfg.on and hold) and hold or "")
end

--[[
    The main screen is the buff list and nothing else.

    Potions used to sit beside it as a peer view, and they are not one: the
    buff list is what you look at while you play, and the potion table is
    something you set up once and then forget. So potions moved in behind the
    gear as a second settings tab, and the front of the panel has no view
    switcher at all — there is only one thing to look at.
]]

    local function tb(key, label)
        return '<div class="tb' .. ((cfg.view == key) and " on" or "")
            .. '" data-mud-action="view" data-mud-data="' .. key .. '">' .. label .. '</div>'
    end
    return tb("set", "settings") .. tb("pots", "potions")
end

--[[
    Settings in, and back out again. Back goes to BUFFS rather than to whatever
    you were on, because a panel with three views whose gear only knows two
    strands you on the third.
]]
local function gear_tab()
    local open = (cfg.view ~= "buffs")
    return '<div class="tb' .. (open and " on" or "")
        .. '" data-mud-action="view" data-mud-data="' .. (open and "buffs" or "set")
        .. '" title="settings">' .. (open and "◀ back" or "⚙") .. '</div>'
end

local function render_buffs()
    local out = ""

    if not have_skills() then
        return '<div class="warn">No skill table yet. It reads one as soon as you are '
            .. 'in the game; REFRESH does it now. That is <code>slist spells</code>, '
            .. 'which is how a skill number becomes a name.</div>'
    end

    if not synced then
        out = out .. '<div class="warn">Not synced yet. It reads <code>aff</code> by itself '
            .. 'once you are in the game — until that lands everything looks down, '
            .. 'including the buffs you are already running, so nothing automatic '
            .. 'happens. SYNC does it now.</div>'
    end

    local rows = buff_rows()

    local anyDown = false
    for _, r in ipairs(rows) do
        if r.up ~= true and r.unknown ~= true then anyDown = true end
    end

    if #rows == 0 then
        return out .. '<div class="note">Nothing running, and no potions in the table yet. '
            .. 'Identify a potion and it turns up under POTIONS.</div>'
    end

    --[[
        Rows, not a table. This panel gets docked in a 190px column and three
        table columns cannot share that — the cells collapse and the buff names
        wrap one character wide. As flex rows the source chip drops onto its
        own line when there is no room for it and nothing else moves.
    ]]
    --[[
        The source is shown for what is DOWN and for nothing else.

        On a buff that is running it is answering a question nobody asked, and
        it answered badly: "no potion set", in red, beside a skill you invoke
        yourself and that has six minutes left on it. It also wrapped, so every
        running buff cost two lines to say one useful thing.
    ]]
    if anyDown then
        out = out .. '<div class="note">Click one that is down to put it back.</div>'
    end

    for _, r in ipairs(rows) do
        local src = (r.up == true) and { text = "", cls = "cast" } or source_of(r)

        --[[
            A row that is DOWN is clickable, and puts that one buff back.

            The whole automatic path is deliberately blunt — 'spellup' casts
            everything and the potion pass picks its own target — so there was
            no way to say "that one, now". This is it, and it is a click on the
            thing itself rather than another button in the corner.

            Rows already up are not clickable: there is nothing to do to them,
            and a control that does nothing is worse than no control.
        ]]
        local click = ""
        if r.up ~= true and r.unknown ~= true then
            click = ' class="brow act" data-mud-action="reup" data-mud-data="'
                .. esc(r.name) .. '" title="put ' .. esc(r.name) .. ' back up"'
        else
            click = ' class="brow"'
        end

        out = out .. '<div' .. click .. '>'
            .. '<span class="nm">' .. esc(r.name) .. '</span>'
            .. '<span class="tm ' .. ((r.up == true) and "up" or "dn")
            .. '" data-mud-bind="' .. esc(bind_key(r)) .. '">'
            .. esc(timer_text(r)) .. '</span>'
            .. ((src.text ~= "")
                and ('<span class="src ' .. src.cls .. '">' .. esc(src.text) .. '</span>')
                or "")
            .. '</div>'
    end

    return out
end

local function render_pots()
    local out = ""

    if seen and not pots[low(seen.keys)] then
        out = out .. '<div class="cand">'
            .. '<span class="nm">' .. esc((seen.name ~= "" and seen.name) or seen.keys) .. '</span>'
            .. '<span class="note">' .. esc(spells_text(seen.spells)) .. '</span>'
            .. '<div class="go" data-mud-action="addseen">add</div>'
            .. '</div>'
    end

    local list = pot_list()

    if #list > 0 then

            .. '<span class="lb">' .. #list .. ' potion'
            .. ((#list == 1) and "" or "s") .. '</span>'
            .. '<span class="sp"></span>'
            .. '<div class="tb" data-mud-action="count" '
            .. 'title="look in the bag and count what is in it">count the bag</div>'
            .. '</div>'
    end

    if #list == 0 then
        out = out .. '<div class="note">No potions yet. Identify one and it appears here — '
            .. 'the box carries the keywords, the item level and the spell level, which is '

    else
        --[[
            One block per potion instead of four table columns. Keywords are a
            long phrase and the spell list is another, and no width this panel

render = function()
    if not widget then return end

    local why = held()

    --[[
        Two rows, always, rather than one that wraps where it feels like.

        left HIDE stranded on a line of its own with a gap beside it. Title and
        state on one row, every control on the next: it costs a line at full
        width and is the same shape at every width, which is the trade worth
        making for a panel that lives in a docked column.

        The state chip is the switch. "switched off" was a label reporting a
        setting you then had to go and find under the gear — and it was also
        the only thing the chip ever said, because held() checks the switch
        first and returns early. So it becomes ON or OFF, green or red, and
        clicking it does the thing it describes.

        The rest of what held() knows is worth keeping, but only when it is
        news: with auto ON and something else stopping it — no skill table, not
        synced, in combat — that reason sits beside the switch. With auto OFF
        it says nothing, because "switched off" next to a button reading OFF is
        not information.
    ]]
    local hold = (cfg.on and why) and why or ""

    local head = '<div class="bar">'
        .. '<span class="ttl">Spellups</span>'
        .. '<div class="tog ' .. (cfg.on and "yes" or "no")

        .. (cfg.on and "on" or "off") .. '</div>'
        .. '<span class="why" data-mud-bind="state">' .. esc(hold) .. '</span>'
        .. '<span class="sp"></span>'
        .. gear_tab()
        .. '</div>'
        --[[
            ONE control row, and what is on it depends on where you are.

            Settings was showing four rows of chrome before any content: title,
            cast-now/hide, the settings tabs, and then COUNT THE BAG. CAST NOW
            is a play-time action and has no business on a settings screen, and
            the settings tabs and HIDE fit on one line together.
        ]]
        .. '<div class="bar btns">'
        .. ((cfg.view == "buffs") and '<span class="sp"></span>'
            .. '<div class="go" data-mud-action="now" '
            .. 'title="cast what you can and quaff one potion for what you cannot, '
            .. 'right now">run now</div>'
            or set_tabs() .. '<span class="sp"></span>')
        .. '<div class="tb" data-mud-action="hide">hide</div>'
        .. '</div>'

    --[[
        Above the view tabs, so it is on screen whichever one you are looking
        at. A shopping reminder that only shows on the potions tab is a
        reminder you see once you have already gone looking.
    ]]
    local lows = low_rows()
    local banner = ""

    if #lows > 0 then
        local bits = {}
        for _, e in ipairs(lows) do
            table.insert(bits, '<span class="it">'
                .. esc((e.row.name ~= "" and e.row.name) or e.row.keys) .. " — "
                .. (e.n <= 0 and "none left" or (e.n .. " left"))
                .. (e.row.where ~= "" and (", bought at " .. esc(e.row.where)) or "")
                .. '</span>')
        end

        banner = '<div class="low"><span class="hd">running low — buy more</span>'
            .. table.concat(bits, "") .. '</div>'
    end

    local body
    if cfg.view == "pots" then
        body = render_pots()
    elseif cfg.view == "set" then
        body = render_set()
    else
        body = render_buffs()
    end

    setWidgetProperty(widget, "content",
        CSS .. '<div class="arc-sp">' .. head .. banner .. body .. '</div>')

--[[
    A button, pressed once, and the only line between these two plugins.

    It reads the Loot Tracker's own stat buckets straight off disk, takes the
    rows whose type is Potion and that recorded a Spells line, and copies them
    into the table above. After that they are this plugin's rows and nothing
    goes back for more — the automatic path never asks the Loot Tracker
    anything, which is the whole point of keeping our own table.
]]
local BUCKETS = { "0", "_" }
for i = 0, 25 do table.insert(BUCKETS, string.char(97 + i)) end

local function loot_installed()
    if type(getLoadedPlugins) ~= "function" then return false end

    local ok, list = pcall(getLoadedPlugins)
    if not ok or type(list) ~= "table" then return false end

    for _, pl in pairs(list) do
        if type(pl) == "table" and pl.id == "aw-loot" and pl.enabled ~= false then
            return true
        end
    end
    return false
end

local function loot_import()
    if not loot_installed() then
        utilprint(TAG .. "$Rthe Loot Tracker isn't installed.$w")
        return
    end

    local added, updated, looked = 0, 0, 0

    for _, letter in ipairs(BUCKETS) do
        local bkt = loadTable("aw_loot_stats_" .. letter, "global")

        if type(bkt) == "table" then
            for _, r in pairs(bkt) do
                if type(r) == "table" then
                    looked = looked + 1

                    local kind = low(tostring(r.type or ""))
                    local keys = trim(tostring(r.keywords or ""))
                    local text = tostring(r.spells or "")

                    if kind == "potion" and keys ~= "" and text ~= "" then
                        local list = {}
                        for _, part in ipairs(split(text, ";")) do
                            local sp = read_spell(part)
                            if sp then table.insert(list, sp) end
                        end

                        if #list > 0 then
                            local had = pots[low(keys)] ~= nil
                            pot_put(keys, tostring(r.item or ""), tonumber(r.level) or 0,
                                    spells_text(list), tostring(r.found_at or r.room or ""))
                            if had then updated = updated + 1 else added = added + 1 end
                        end
                    end
                end
            end
        end
    end

    utilprint(TAG .. "read " .. looked .. " item(s) from the Loot Tracker: "
        .. added .. " potion(s) added, " .. updated .. " updated.")
    render()
end

--[[
    Pull a quoted phrase off the front of a string, because a potion's keywords
    are a phrase and everything after them is not. 'pot add "a b c" fly 1'
    would otherwise be six arguments with no way to tell where the first ends.
]]
local function take_quoted(s)
    s = trim(s)
    local a = string.sub(s, 1, 1)

    if a == '"' or a == "'" then
        local e = string.find(string.sub(s, 2), a, 1, true)
        if e then
            return { head = trim(string.sub(s, 2, e)),
                     rest = trim(string.sub(s, e + 2)) }
        end
    end

    local sp = string.find(s, " ", 1, true)
    if not sp then return { head = s, rest = "" } end
    return { head = trim(string.sub(s, 1, sp - 1)),
             rest = trim(string.sub(s, sp + 1)) }
end

--[[
    Keep a potion that was identified this session.

    With keywords, that exact one — which is what the link under each box
    sends, so three boxes leave three working offers. Without, the last one
    seen, which is what the panel's ADD button and a bare 'awbuff add' mean.
]]
local function add_seen(keys)
    local b = seen

    keys = unquote(keys or "")
    if keys ~= "" then b = seenBox[low(keys)] end

    if type(b) ~= "table" then
        utilprint(TAG .. (keys ~= ""
            and ("$Rnothing identified with those keywords this session.$w")
            or  ("$Rnothing identified yet — 'id <potion>' and try again.$w")))
        return
    end

    pot_put(b.keys, b.name, b.level, spells_text(b.spells), b.where)
    utilprint(TAG .. "added " .. ((b.name ~= "" and b.name) or b.keys)
        .. " — " .. spells_pretty(pots[low(b.keys)]) .. ".")
    render()
end

local function pot_cmd(rest)
    local cut  = take_quoted(rest)
    local verb, tail = low(cut.head), cut.rest

    if verb == "add" then
        local cut2 = take_quoted(tail)
        local keys, more = cut2.head, cut2.rest
        if keys == "" then
            utilprint(TAG .. 'awbuff pot add "<keywords>" <spell> <level>')
            return
        end

        -- the level is the last word, the spell is everything before it
        local words = argv(more)
        local lvl   = tonumber(words[#words])
        if not lvl or #words < 2 then
            utilprint(TAG .. 'awbuff pot add "<keywords>" <spell name> <spell level>')
            utilprint("$K  The level is the SPELL's, off the \"1 use of level 5 'detect "
                .. "invis'\" line.$w")
            return
        end

        local spell = {}
        for i = 1, #words - 1 do table.insert(spell, words[i]) end
        spell = trim(table.concat(spell, " "))

        local row = pots[low(keys)]
        local list = row and spells_of(row) or {}

        -- same spell twice on one potion is an edit, not a second entry
        local hit = false
        for _, sp in ipairs(list) do
            if low(sp.name) == low(spell) then sp.level = lvl; hit = true end
        end
        if not hit then table.insert(list, { level = lvl, name = spell }) end

        pot_put(keys, row and row.name or "", row and row.level or 0,
                spells_text(list), row and row.where or "")

        utilprint(TAG .. '"' .. keys .. '" casts ' .. spells_pretty(pots[low(keys)]) .. ".")
        render()

    elseif verb == "del" or verb == "rm" then
        local keys = take_quoted(tail).head
        local k = low(keys)
        if pots[k] then
            pots = forget(pots, k)
            clear_row(k)
            pots_save()
            utilprint(TAG .. "forgot \"" .. keys .. "\".")
            render()
        else
            utilprint(TAG .. "$Rno potion with those keywords.$w")
        end

    elseif verb == "on" or verb == "off" then
        local keys = take_quoted(tail).head
        local r = pots[low(keys)]
        if type(r) ~= "table" then
            utilprint(TAG .. "$Rno potion with those keywords.$w")
            return
        end

        r.on = (verb == "on")
        if r.on then clear_row(low(keys)) end
        pots_save()
        render()
        utilprint(TAG .. ((r.name ~= "" and r.name) or r.keys) .. " " .. verb .. ".")

    elseif verb == "where" then
        local cut3 = take_quoted(tail)
        local keys, w = cut3.head, cut3.rest
        local r = pots[low(keys)]
        if type(r) ~= "table" then
            utilprint(TAG .. "$Rno potion with those keywords.$w")
            return
        end
        r.where = trim(w)
        pots_save()
        render()
        utilprint(TAG .. "bought at: " .. (r.where ~= "" and r.where or "(cleared)"))

    else
        utilprint(TAG .. 'awbuff pot add|del|on|off|where "<keywords>" ...')
    end
end

local function cmd(args)
    local a = argv(args)
    local verb = low(a[1] or "")

    local rest = ""
    for i = 2, #a do rest = rest .. (rest == "" and "" or " ") .. a[i] end

    if verb == "" then
        showWidget(widget)
        render()

    elseif verb == "on" or verb == "off" then
        cfg.on = (verb == "on")
        quiet, run = false, 0
        if cfg.on then enable_tags() end
        save_cfg()
        render()

        local why = held()
        utilprint(TAG .. "$G" .. verb .. "$w"
            .. ((cfg.on and why) and (" — but holding: " .. why) or "."))

    elseif verb == "now" then
        run_now()

    elseif verb == "go" then
        --[[
            qpend as well, and that is the whole point of this verb.

            An in-flight quaff blocks everything for QGRACE seconds, so a 'go'
            that cleared the stand-down but left a phantom entry behind did
            nothing at all for twelve seconds and gave no sign why. If you are
            telling it to carry on, nothing is in flight any more.
        ]]
        quiet, run = false, 0
        stock, qpend = {}, {}
        render()
        utilprint(TAG .. "carrying on.")

    elseif verb == "refresh" then
        if not playing() then
            utilprint(TAG .. "$Rnot in the game yet.$w")
        else
            utilprint(TAG .. "reading the skill table...")
            enable_tags(true)
            send("slist spells")
        end

    elseif verb == "sync" then
        sync()

    elseif verb == "prefer" then
        local k = low(rest)
        if k ~= "cast" and k ~= "level" then
            utilprint(TAG .. "awbuff prefer cast | level   (now: " .. cfg.prefer .. ")")
            utilprint("$K  cast  - cast what you know; potions only for what you can't$w")
            utilprint("$K  level - whichever lands the better buff, cast or potion$w")
            return
        end

        cfg.prefer = k
        save_cfg()
        render()
        utilprint(TAG .. (k == "level"
            and "takes whichever lands the better buff."
            or  "casts what you know; potions only for what you can't."))

    elseif verb == "potions" or verb == "usepots" then
        cfg.potions = not cfg.potions
        save_cfg()
        render()
        utilprint(TAG .. (cfg.potions
            and "may spend potions by itself."
            or  "casts only; clicking a buff is the only thing that drinks one."))

    elseif verb == "login" then
        cfg.login = not cfg.login
        save_cfg()
        render()
        utilprint(TAG .. (cfg.login
            and "reads the skill table and 'aff' once you're in the game."
            or  "$Rsends nothing on login — 'awbuff refresh' and 'awbuff sync' by hand.$w"))

    elseif verb == "list" then
        list_spellups()

    elseif verb == "pots" or verb == "potions" then
        show_pots()

    elseif verb == "add" then
        add_seen(rest)

    elseif verb == "pot" then
        pot_cmd(rest)

    elseif verb == "import" then
        loot_import()

    --[[
        Ask the MUD what's in the bag. The listing triggers pick the numbers
        back up, so this sends one command and reads the answer rather than
        polling — which is why the counts are then kept by subtraction instead
        of being asked for again.
    ]]
    elseif verb == "count" then
        if trim(cfg.bag) == "" then
            utilprint(TAG .. "$Rno potion bag set — 'awbuff bag <keywords>'.$w")
        elseif not playing() then
            utilprint(TAG .. "$Rnot in the game yet.$w")
        else
            lowSaid = {}
            send('look in "' .. cfg.bag .. '"')
        end

    --[[
        The same four numbers the panel's steppers set, from the keyboard.

        One verb rather than four, because they are one kind of thing and a
        wrong name should answer with the list rather than with help for the
        whole plugin. Bounded by LIMITS either way — there is no route in here
        that accepts a number this thing won't act on.
    ]]
    elseif verb == "set" then
        local words = argv(rest)
        local key   = low(words[1] or "")
        local n     = (words[2] and words[2] ~= "") and tonumber(words[2]) or nil

        if not LIMITS[key] or not n then
            local names = {}
            for k, L in pairs(LIMITS) do
                table.insert(names, k .. " " .. L.lo .. "-" .. L.hi
                    .. " (now " .. cfg[k] .. ")")
            end
            table.sort(names)

            utilprint(TAG .. "awbuff set <name> <n>")
            for _, s in ipairs(names) do utilprint("$K  " .. s .. "$w") end
            return
        end

        cfg[key] = clamp(key, math.floor(n))
        -- moving the line re-arms every warning; the old ones were answers to
        -- a different question
        if key == "low" then lowSaid = {} end

        save_cfg()
        render()
        utilprint(TAG .. key .. " = " .. cfg[key] .. "  (" .. LIMITS[key].note .. ")")

    elseif verb == "bag" then
        cfg.bag = unquote(rest)
        save_cfg()
        render()
        utilprint(TAG .. (cfg.bag ~= ""
            and ('potions come out of "' .. cfg.bag .. '".')
            or "no bag — potions are assumed to be on you."))

    elseif verb == "why" then
        local id = byname[low(rest)] or tonumber(rest)
        local s  = id and skills[id]
        if type(s) ~= "table" then
            utilprint(TAG .. "$Rdon't know a spell called '" .. rest .. "'.$w")
            return
        end

        local f = failed[id]
        if type(f) ~= "table" then
            utilprint(TAG .. s.name .. ": nothing failed recently.")
            return
        end

        local d = FAIL[f.code or 0]
        utilprint(TAG .. s.name .. ": " .. (d and d[1] or ("code " .. tostring(f.code)))
            .. ", " .. (now() - f.at) .. "s ago.")

        local p = pot_for(s.name)
        if p then
            utilprint("$K  potion: " .. ((p.row.name ~= "" and p.row.name) or p.row.keys)
                .. " at level " .. p.level .. "$w")
        end

    --[[
        What it actually thinks, rather than what the panel shows.

        Written because a screenshot of a perfect identify box next to a panel
        saying "no potions yet" contains no information about which of the four
        stages between them failed. Run it right after an 'id'.
    ]]
    elseif verb == "raw" then
        utilprint(TAG .. "state")
        utilprint("$K  cast " .. ((now() < castDead)
            and ("held " .. (castDead - now()) .. "s: the MUD had nothing to cast")
            or ("ready, " .. downcount() .. " castable buff(s) down")))
        utilprint("$K  cast " .. ((now() < castDead)
            and ("held " .. (castDead - now()) .. "s: the MUD had nothing to cast")
            or ("ready, " .. downcount() .. " castable buff(s) down")))
        utilprint("$K  retry " .. (retryAt > 0 and (retryWhy .. " in "
            .. math.max(0, retryAt - now()) .. "s") or "none")
            .. "   used " .. retries .. "/" .. RETRY_MAX)
        utilprint("$K  skills " .. skills_count() .. "   synced " .. tostring(synced)
            .. "   tags sent " .. tostring(tagsSent) .. "   in game " .. tostring(playing())
            .. "   auto " .. tostring(cfg.on) .. "   holding: " .. (held() or "nothing"))

        utilprint(TAG .. "identify box")
        utilprint("$K  start lines " .. dbg.start .. "   rows " .. dbg.rows
            .. "   ends " .. dbg.ends)
        utilprint("$K  last: " .. dbg.last)
        utilprint("$K  verdict: " .. (dbg.why ~= "" and dbg.why or "-"))

        if dbg.start == 0 then
            utilprint("$R  The 'Keywords' line never matched. That is the whole problem "
                .. "— nothing downstream ran.$w")
        end

        utilprint(TAG .. "buffs (" .. pot_count() .. " potion(s) in the table)")
        local rows = buff_rows()
        if #rows == 0 then
            utilprint("$K  none")
        end
        for _, r in ipairs(rows) do
            local src = source_of(r).text
            utilprint("$K  " .. r.name .. "   id=" .. tostring(r.id)
                .. " up=" .. tostring(r.up) .. " secs=" .. tostring(r.secs)
                .. " unknown=" .. tostring(r.unknown) .. "  -> " .. src)
        end

    elseif verb == "hide" then
        hideWidget(widget)

    else
        help()
    end
end

function init()
    local saved = loadTable(VAR)
    if type(saved) == "table" then
        if saved.on == true     then cfg.on = true end
        if saved.combat == true then cfg.combat = true end

        -- default ON, so this one tests for the switch-off rather than the
        -- switch-on: a missing key has to mean the default, not false
        if saved.login == false then cfg.login = false end

        if type(saved.bag)  == "string" then cfg.bag  = saved.bag end
        if type(saved.view) == "string" then cfg.view = saved.view end

        for key in pairs(LIMITS) do
            local n = tonumber(saved[key])
            if n then cfg[key] = clamp(key, math.floor(n)) end
        end
    end

    -- the durable copy wins: saveTable is wiped by the remove-and-re-add that
    -- installs every update, and this one is not
    cfg_load()

    for key in pairs(LIMITS) do cfg[key] = clamp(key, tonumber(cfg[key]) or LIMITS[key].lo) end

    local nSkills = load_skills()
    local nPots   = pots_load()

    haveLoot = loot_installed()

    widget = createWidget({
        type     = "html",
        name     = "spellups",
        title    = "Spellups",
        position = { x = 140, y = 140 },
        size     = { width = 430, height = 480 },
        visible  = false,
        appearance = {
            showTitleBar        = false,
            autoHideSettingsCog = true,
        },
    })

    --[[
        Clear first. init() runs again on every hot-reload and
        registerWidgetEvent APPENDS — so each reload stacks another handler on
        the same widget and one click fires all of them. It shows up as buttons
        sending their command two, three, five times, getting worse the longer
        a session goes on, and nothing about it looks like a plugin bug from
        the outside.

        unregisterWidgetEvent with no callback drops every handler for the
        event, which is exactly what a fresh init wants.
    ]]
    drop_handlers(widget, "action")
    registerWidgetEvent(widget, "action", function(data)
        if type(data) ~= "table" then return end

        local what = tostring(data.action or "")
        local key = tostring(data.data or "")

        if what == "hide" then
            hideWidget(widget)
            return

        elseif what == "view" then
            cfg.view = key
            save_cfg()

        elseif what == "auto" then
            cfg.on = not cfg.on
            quiet, run = false, 0
            if cfg.on then enable_tags() end
            save_cfg()

        elseif what == "potauto" then
            cfg.potions = not cfg.potions
            save_cfg()

        elseif what == "combat" then
            cfg.combat = not cfg.combat
            save_cfg()

        elseif what == "prefer" then
            cfg.prefer = (key == "level") and "level" or "cast"
            save_cfg()
    
        elseif what == "login" then
            cfg.login = not cfg.login
            save_cfg()

        elseif what == "now" then
            run_now()
            quiet, run = false, 0

        elseif what == "refresh" then
            if playing() then
                enable_tags(true)
                send("slist spells")
            else
                utilprint(TAG .. "$Rnot in the game yet.$w")
            end

        elseif what == "sync" then
            sync()

        elseif what == "import" then
            loot_import()

        elseif what == "count" then
            if trim(cfg.bag) == "" then
                utilprint(TAG .. "$Rno potion bag set — set one under the gear.$w")
            elseif playing() then
                lowSaid = {}
                send('look in "' .. cfg.bag .. '"')
            end

        --[[
            One buff, put back, by whichever route would have handled it.

            This is the one place a single spell is cast by name — everywhere
            else it is the MUD's own 'spellup', which picks better than we can.
            Here you have already picked, so casting the whole list would be
            answering a different question.
        ]]
        elseif what == "reup" then
            local id = byname[low(key)]

            if not id then
                utilprint(TAG .. "$Rdon't know a spell called '" .. key .. "'.$w")

            elseif not playing() then
                utilprint(TAG .. "$Rnot in the game yet.$w")

            elseif cast_why(id) == "" then
                send("cast '" .. key .. "'")
                utilprint(TAG .. "casting " .. key .. ".")

            else
                local p = pot_for(key)
                if p then
                    quaff(p.row, key .. ", by hand")
                else
                    utilprint(TAG .. "$Rcan't cast " .. key
                        .. " and no potion is set for it.$w")
                end
            end

        elseif what == "addseen" then
            add_seen()

        elseif what == "potdel" then
            pots = forget(pots, low(key))
            clear_row(low(key))
            pots_save()

        elseif what == "poton" then
            local r = pots[low(key)]
            if type(r) == "table" then
                r.on = (r.on == false)
                if r.on then clear_row(low(key)) end
                pots_save()
            end

        elseif what == "inc" or what == "dec" then
            local L = LIMITS[key]
            if not L then return end

            local step = (what == "inc") and L.step or -L.step
            cfg[key] = clamp(key, (tonumber(cfg[key]) or L.lo) + step)
            if key == "low" then lowSaid = {} end
            save_cfg()
        end

        shape = nil
        render()
    end)

    drop_handlers(widget, "submit")
    registerWidgetEvent(widget, "submit", function(data)
        if type(data) ~= "table" then return end

        local f = data.formData
        if type(f) ~= "table" then return end

        if type(f.bag) == "string" then
            cfg.bag = unquote(f.bag)
            save_cfg()
            utilprint(TAG .. (cfg.bag ~= ""
                and ('potions come out of "' .. cfg.bag .. '".')
                or "no bag — potions are assumed to be on you."))
        end

        if type(f.keys) == "string" and unquote(f.keys) ~= "" then
            local keys  = unquote(f.keys)
            local spell = trim(tostring(f.spell or ""))
            local lvl   = tonumber(trim(tostring(f.level or "")))

            if spell == "" or not lvl then
                utilprint(TAG .. "$Rneed a spell name and its level.$w")
            else
                local row  = pots[low(keys)]
                local list = row and spells_of(row) or {}

                local hit = false
                for _, sp in ipairs(list) do
                    if low(sp.name) == low(spell) then sp.level = lvl; hit = true end
                end
                if not hit then table.insert(list, { level = lvl, name = spell }) end

                pot_put(keys, row and row.name or "", row and row.level or 0,
                        spells_text(list), trim(tostring(f.where or "")))
                utilprint(TAG .. '"' .. keys .. '" casts '
                    .. spells_pretty(pots[low(keys)]) .. ".")
            end
        end

        shape = nil
        render()
    end)

    --[[
        Every trigger is registered here, once, and gated on state.

        A trigger created while a packet is being processed does not apply to
        lines already in that packet — and an slist block, an 'aff' listing and
        an identify box all arrive whole. Arming a row reader from the opening
        line means reading the opening line and nothing else.
    ]]
    addTrigger("^\\{spellheaders", on_spellheaders, { type = "regex", keepEvaluating = true })
    addTrigger("^\\{recoveries",   on_recoveries,   { type = "regex", keepEvaluating = true })
    addTrigger("^\\{/(?:spellheaders|recoveries)", on_ingest_end,
        { type = "regex", keepEvaluating = true })
    addTrigger("^(\\d+,.+)$", on_ingest_row, { type = "regex", keepEvaluating = true })

    addTrigger("^\\{affon\\}(\\d+),(\\d+)", on_affon, { type = "regex", keepEvaluating = true })
    addTrigger("^\\{affoff\\}(\\d+)", on_affoff, { type = "regex", keepEvaluating = true })
    addTrigger("^\\{sfail\\}(-?\\d+),(\\d+),(\\d+),(-?\\d+)", on_sfail,
        { type = "regex", keepEvaluating = true })
    addTrigger("^\\{recon\\}(\\d+),(\\d+)", on_recon, { type = "regex", keepEvaluating = true })
    addTrigger("^\\{recoff\\}(\\d+)", on_recoff, { type = "regex", keepEvaluating = true })
    addTrigger("^\\{skillgain\\}(\\d+),(\\d+)", on_skillgain,
        { type = "regex", keepEvaluating = true })

    --[[
        The 'aff' reply. No header trigger opens the window any more — sync()
        does that when it sends — so these only have to read rows and notice
        the end, and getting a wording wrong costs a sync rather than wedging
        the plugin shut forever.

        The row pattern takes everything after the colon and lets read_clock
        find the time in it, because Aardwolf prints at least four different
        shapes there and "+3" has to fall out as "not an affect".
    ]]
    addTrigger("^\\s+(?:You have the following|special affects|skill/spell modifiers)",
        on_aff_section, { type = "regex", keepEvaluating = true })
    addTrigger("^You have the following", on_aff_section,
        { type = "regex", keepEvaluating = true })
    addTrigger("^You are affected by the following", on_aff_open,
        { type = "regex", keepEvaluating = true })
    addTrigger("^ {2,}(\\S.*?)\\s*:\\s*(.+?)\\s*$", on_aff_row,
        { type = "regex", keepEvaluating = true })
    --[[
        'affected by \\d', not 'affected by '. The count line is "You are
        affected by 12 skills/spells." but the SPELLS HEADER may well be "You
        are affected by the following skills/spells:" — and a pattern loose
        enough to take both would close the sync window on the header, before a
        single row had been read. Caught by check-regex.py, which is the entire
        reason that file exists.
    ]]
    addTrigger("^You are (?:not affected|affected by \\d)", on_aff_end,
        { type = "regex", keepEvaluating = true })
    addTrigger("^Use 'saffects'", on_aff_tail,
        { type = "regex", keepEvaluating = true })
    --[[
        The catch-all that hides the body of a sync we asked for. Priority 30,
        below every reader, so the rows are parsed before the line is dropped —
        and it does nothing at all unless a hidden block is open, which is
        almost always.
    ]]
    addTrigger("^.*$", on_aff_gag, { type = "regex", priority = 30, keepEvaluating = true })

    --[[
        The identify box. Reads what already scrolled past and sends nothing,
        so identifying a potion for any other reason fills the table in as a
        side effect. The two catch-alls do a nil check and return when no box
        is open, which is almost always.
    ]]
    --[[
        Deliberately loose. The strict form wants exactly one space after the
        pipe and a pipe at the end of the line, and neither is worth betting
        the whole feature on — a box padded differently, or one whose closing
        pipe is followed by a space, silently captures nothing at all and there
        is no error anywhere. Everything after the colon is the keywords.
    ]]
    --[[
        One trigger per field. The splitting happens in the regex engine, which
        works, rather than in a hand-written parser over string.find, which did
        not — see read_spell for what that cost.

        Every pattern tolerates padding and a missing trailing pipe, because a
        box drawn slightly differently must not silently capture nothing.
    ]]
    addTrigger("^\\|\\s*Keywords\\s*:\\s*(.+?)\\s*\\|?\\s*$", on_box_start,
        { type = "regex", keepEvaluating = true })
    addTrigger("^\\|\\s*Name\\s*:\\s*(.+?)\\s*\\|?\\s*$", on_box_name,
        { type = "regex", keepEvaluating = true })
    addTrigger("^\\|\\s*Type\\s*:\\s*(\\S+)(?:.*?Level\\s*:\\s*(\\d+))?", on_box_type,
        { type = "regex", keepEvaluating = true })
    addTrigger("^\\|\\s*Spells\\s*:\\s*(.+?)\\s*\\|?\\s*$", on_box_spells,
        { type = "regex", keepEvaluating = true })
    addTrigger("^\\|\\s*:\\s*(.+?)\\s*\\|?\\s*$", on_box_more,
        { type = "regex", keepEvaluating = true })
    addTrigger("^[^|+].*$", on_box_end, { type = "regex", priority = 40, keepEvaluating = true })

    addTrigger("^No spells or skills cast\\.$", on_nothing_cast,
        { type = "regex", keepEvaluating = true })
    addTrigger("^You do not have that item\\.$", on_no_item,
        { type = "regex", keepEvaluating = true })
    addTrigger("^You don't have that potion\\.$", on_no_item,
        { type = "regex", keepEvaluating = true })

    --[[
        Counting the bag. 'look in <bag>' opens a listing, the rows inside it
        carry the numbers, and every quaff takes one off. The row trigger is a
        catch-all gated on being inside OUR bag — inventory and every other
        container print the same shape, and counting the wrong one would report
        two potions with ninety in the bag.
    ]]
    addTrigger("^(?:The )?(.+) contains:$", on_bag_start,
        { type = "regex", keepEvaluating = true })
    addTrigger("^You are carrying:$", function() inBag = false end,
        { type = "regex", keepEvaluating = true })
    --[[
        Two patterns rather than one with an optional count, and this is not
        tidiness.

        cap() works out whether captures arrived 0- or 1-based by looking at
        whether the first one is a string. A leading group that didn't
        participate is not a string, so the base comes out as 1 and every
        lookup shifts by one — asking for the quantity hands back the item
        name. An optional group anywhere but last poisons that inference, so
        there isn't one.
    ]]
    addTrigger("^\\(\\s*(\\d+)\\)\\s+(.+)$", on_bag_line,
        { type = "regex", priority = 40, keepEvaluating = true })
    addTrigger("^(?!\\()\\s*(\\S.*)$", on_bag_single,
        { type = "regex", priority = 40, keepEvaluating = true })
    addTrigger("^You quaff (.+)\\.$", on_quaff,
        { type = "regex", keepEvaluating = true })

    addTrigger("^Your primary class is now \\w+\\.$", on_classchange,
        { type = "regex", keepEvaluating = true })
    addTrigger("^\\* Remort transformation complete!$", on_remort,
        { type = "regex", keepEvaluating = true })
    addTrigger("^You see your own dead body from above\\.$", on_death,
        { type = "regex", keepEvaluating = true })

    --[[
        Core sends the union of what every plugin declares. Never send
        Core.Supports.Set from here — Aardwolf REPLACES its record of your
        subscriptions on receipt, so a second sender silently unsubscribes
        everything missing from its own list.
    ]]
    broadcastPlugin("aw-gmcp", "Char")

    --[[
        char.status is how this finds out you're in the game. Both spellings,
        because which case the client hands back has not been consistent.
    ]]
    onGMCPUpdate("char.status", on_status)
    onGMCPUpdate("Char.Status", on_status)

    registerCommand("awbuff", cmd,
        "buff manager: casts what you can cast, quaffs what you can't")

    --[[
        Two clocks. The panel's is a second, because it draws countdowns; the
        decision's is slower, because nothing here is improved by being decided
        five times a second and a potion is not a thing to be eager about.
    ]]
    addTimer(1000, tick_panel, true)
    addTimer(2000, decide, true)

    render()

    utilprint(TAG .. nSkills .. " skills from cache, " .. nPots .. " potion(s). "
        .. (cfg.login and "Reads what's on you once you're in."
                      or "'awbuff sync' once you're in."))
end

function cleanup()
    save_skills()
    pots_save()
end
